GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 750 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
WATER SECURITY PLAN 
†750.  Dr. SAMBIT PATRA: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any water security plan and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has implemented any pilo t projects under the said plan in various States of  the 
country and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has received any proposa ls from the State Governments seeking technical and  
financial assistance under the said plan and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has revised the existing  policy relating to the sources of funding and fina ncing 
mechanism for implementation of the said plan and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether any proposal to accord priority to the districts identified in the Aspirational Districts Programme 
for the water security plan is under consideration of the Government and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) to (e) Water, being a State subject, sustainable developme nt and management of water and groundwater 
resources, including preparation of Water Security Plans, is primarily the responsibility of the State  
Governments. However, the Central Government facili tates the efforts of the State Governments by way o f 
technical and financial assistance through its vari ous schemes and projects. The major steps taken in this 
direction are as under:- 
i. Under Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA), more than 2 crore w ater conservation and artificial recharge works 
have been taken up through convergence in the count ry so far, which has played a key role in 
enhancing the sustainability of ground water resources in water-stressed districts. 
ii. To further strengthen the momentum of JSA, Jal Sanc hay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative has been 
launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in 2024 with  a vision to make rainwater harvesting a mass 
movement in the country. By promoting community own ership and responsibility, the initiative 
seeks to develop cost-eﬀective, local solutions tai lored to speciﬁc water challenges across districts.  
Thus far, more than 1.55 crore artificial groundwat er recharge and storage works have been 
constructed across the country under this initiativ e. Subsequently, on 01.06.2026 JSJB-Catch The 
Rain (CTR) has been launched nation-wide for water conservation and artificial recharge. 
iii. Ministry of Jal Shakti has successfully demonstrate d the efficacy of community-led participatory 
groundwater management through Atal Bhujal Yojana, which was implemented on pilot basis in 

2 
 
8,203 water stressed Gram Panchayats of 229 Blocks across the seven participating States – Gujarat, 
Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Ra jasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Under the 
scheme, sustainable water resource management was p romoted through a combination of scientific 
monitoring, community participation and demand-and supply-side interventions. Major 
activities/works undertaken under the Scheme are mentioned below:  
 Measurement and public disclosure of groundwater data have been made across all 8,203 Atal 
Jal Gram Panchayats (GPs) of all 7 states through physical as well as electronic means. 
 Community-led Water Budgets and Water Security Plans have been prepared by all GPs of all 
7 states and updated annually. 
 More than 1.28 lakh GP-level trainings have been co nducted, alongside Block, District and 
State-level capacity-building trainings. 
 Piezometers along with Digital Water Level Recorder s and Rain Gauges have been installed 
in almost all GPs under the Yojana. 
 Monitoring of around 70,000 wells at GP level, with data shared publicly. 
 Mapping of over 99,000 existing water conservation and artificial recharge structures 
 More than 83,800 supply-side structures like check dams, ponds, recharge shafts/pits etc. have 
been constructed/renovated for water conservation and groundwater recharge across 7 states. 
 Around 9.7 lakh hectares have been brought under ef ficient water-use practices (drip/ 
sprinkler irrigation, mulching, crop diversification, etc.) across 7 states. 
iv. Mission Amrit Sarovar, 2022 was launched by the Gov ernment of India which aimed at developing 
and rejuvenating at least 75 water bodies in each d istrict of the country. Nearly 69,000 Amrit 
Sarovars have been constructed/rejuvenated in the c ountry leading to enhanced water storage and 
ground water recharge. 
v. The Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare ha s been implementing the Per Drop More Crop 
component since 2015-16 to improve on-farm water-us e efficiency through micro-irrigation. The 
scheme supports efficient irrigation practices in d istricts across the country, thereby reducing 
groundwater extraction and promoting sustainable use of groundwater resources. 
vi. Under NAQUIM 1.0, country's aquifers were mapped ma cro-level understanding of our nation's 
groundwater resources were developed. Under NAQUIM 2.0 state-of-the-art technologies are 
harnessed, for generating highly detailed scientifi c data which serve as an important tool for making 
informed decisions for sustainable groundwater management. 
vii. The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched during the year 2015-16, with 
the aim to enhance physical access of water on farm  and expand cultivable area under assured 
irrigation, improve on-farm water use efficiency, i ntroduce sustainable water conservation practices, 
etc.  30.66 lakh hectare irrigation potential has b een created, with pari passu development of 23.42 
lakh hectare command area has been achieved under t he Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme 
and Command Area Development & Water Management components of PMKSY. 
viii. CGWB has also prepared the Master Plan for Artifici al Recharge to Groundwater- 2020 for the 
entire country and shared it with States/UTs. The M aster Plan serves as a technical guide for 
planning and implementation of rainwater harvesting  and artificial recharge structures in districts 
based on local hydrogeological conditions.

(a) whether the Government has fixed any target for providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections to

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 752 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026  
CONSTRUCTION OF NATIONAL HIGHWAY PROJECTS 
  
752.    SHRI RAHUL KASWAN:  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government has conducted any comprehensive evaluation 
regarding progress, cost, timelines and regional balance of the Bharatmala 
Pariyojana, Economic Corridors and other National Highway projects during the 
last three years and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the details of National Highway projects sanctioned, under construction and 
completed, State-wise including Rajasthan;  
(c) whether th e Government has reviewed the projects delayed due to land 
acquisition, forest clearances, utility shifting and other reasons and if so, the 
major reasons therefor and the solutions proposed therein; and  
(d) the new monitoring and project management syste ms developed by the 
Government to ensure the timely completion of National Highway projects? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) and (b) Bharatmala Pariyojana  Phase-I was approved by the Government   in 
2017, covering a length of 34,800 km across the Country at an estimated outlay 
of Rs. 5,35,000 Crore. Under the programme, projects covering a total length of 
26,425 km had been awarded. Out of this, 22,709 km ha ve already been 
constructed as of May 2026. State -wise details of the projects under 
Bharatmala Pariyojana are enclosed at Annexure-I. 
  
A study conducted by the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), 
Bangalore, to evaluate the impact of Bharatmala Pariyoja na indicates positive 
effects across multiple sectors. Economically, household income and 

expenditure have increased. Logistics efficiency has improved with reduced 
costs. Businesses have benefited from better access to markets and factories. 
Socially, tra vel time to schools and healthcare facilities has decreased, 
enhancing accessibility. Overall, the study suggests that Bharatmala 
Pariyojana has significantly contributed to socio-economic growth.  
  
The details of National Highway projects/length sanction ed, under 
construction and completed, State -wise including Rajasthan during the last 
three years are enclosed at Annexure-II, Annexure-III and Annexure-IV 
respectively. 
  
(c) The primary reasons for delay in National Highway (NH) projects are 
issues/bottlenecks relating to land acquisition, delay in getting statutory 
clearances, utility shifting, encroachment removal, law & order, non-availability 
of construction material/minerals, poor performance of 
Contractor/Concessionaire, and Force Majeur e events like the Covid -19 
pandemic etc. 
  
To expedite project execution, various initiatives have been undertaken, 
including streamlining the land acquisition process through the Bhoomi Rashi 
Portal, revamping the Parivesh Portal through Ministry of Envir onment, Forests 
& Climate Change (MoEFCC) to expedite forest and environmental clearances, 
enabling online approval of General Arrangement Drawings (GAD) for Road Over 
Bridges (ROBs) and Road Under Bridges (RUBs) from the Railways, and 
conducting review me etings at various levels with all stakeholders, including 
State Governments. The National Highway projects are regularly reviewed and 
monitored at various levels including through the Project Monitoring Group and 
"PRAGATI". 
  
(d)    Further, monitoring of NH projects is being done through Data Lake 3.0, a 
centralized GIS -based platform covering pre -construction, construction, and 
operation & maintenance stages. Data Lake 3.0 is scheduled to be fully 
operational by April 2027. 
 
Further, Artificial Intelligen ce/Machine Learning (AI/ML) -enabled drone 
monitoring is being used to validate physical progress through geo -tagged 
imagery and GIS-based dashboards integrated with the Data Lake.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 753 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
OUTCOME ASSESSMENT OF SCADA-IOT BASED IRRIGATION SYSTEMS 
753. Shri DUSHYANT SINGH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has initiated any outcom e-based evaluation framework for SCADA-IoT based 
irrigation systems under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) and the Modernisation of 
Command Area Development and Water Management (MCAD WM) Scheme to assess improvements in 
water use efficiency, energy savings, irrigation reliability and crop productivity, particularly across the thirty-
two sanctioned clusters and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any baseline performance indicators hav e been prescribed for States to measure water savin gs, 
reduction in transmission losses and improvement in command area coverage and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the steps being taken to develop replicable nat ional models and best practice benchmarks across di fferent 
agro-climatic zones as envisaged by the Government for scaling technology-enabled irrigation 
modernisation; and 
(d) whether the findings from the pilot clusters in cluding the Bisalpur Right Main Canal cluster in Ra jasthan 
are proposed to be used for a broader national irrigation modernisation roadmap and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a)  Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was  launched during the year 2015-16, with an aim 
to enhance physical access of water on farm and expand cultivable area under assured irrigation, improve on-
farm water use efficiency, introduce sustainable water conservation practices, etc.  Technological innovations 
such as underground pipelines, micro-irrigation, SC ADA based monitoring etc. are promoted under Pradha n 
Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana- Accelerated Irrigat ion Benefits Programme (PMKSY-AIBP). States are 
encouraged to adopt such interventions for enhanced  water use efficiency. The list of some of the impo rtant 
projects under PMKSY-AIBP with SCADA as a component is at Annexure - I. 
Further, the Cabinet approved the Modernization of Command Area Development and Water 
Management (M-CADWM) as a sub-scheme of PMKSY on 09 .04.2025 for the period 2025-2026 to be 
implemented on pilot projects basis. The Scheme env isages monitoring of water use efficiency, water 
accounting and other performance parameters using S CADA, Internet of Things (IoT) and satellite-based 
technologies across the 38 sanctioned pilot cluster s. Total 38 nos. of such projects spreading over in  28 
States/UTs have been sanctioned ( Annexure-II ). 

2 
 
 
Water being State subject, it is for the State Gove rnment concerned to plan, implement and manage 
the irrigation projects, and to prepare action plan  to make irrigation system more extensive in the St ate. The 
role of Government of India is limited to providing  technical support, and partial ﬁnancial assistance  for 
identiﬁed projects under the ongoing schemes. 
(b)  The Modernization of Command Area Development and Water Management (M-CADWM) scheme 
provides for baseline indicators which include, cro pping intensity, water use efficiency, water produc tivity, 
farmers' participation, adoption of micro-irrigatio n and energy efficiency etc. During the Operation a nd 
Management phase, water use efficiency, water accou nting and other performance parameters are monitore d 
through SCADA, IoT and satellite-based systems.  
(c)  The M-CADWM Scheme envisages implementation of pil ot projects across different agro-climatic zones 
in the country incorporating institutional, technic al and management reforms and strategies in the com mand 
area development  and water management. Based on th e learnings in design and structuring of these 
projects, National Programme for Modernisation of C ommand Area Development and Water Management 
will be designed. In this regard, total 38 nos. of such projects in 28 States/UTs has been sanctioned for 
implementation (Annexure-II).  
(d)  Yes, based on the learnings in design and structuring of the 38 pilot clusters, including the Bisalpur Right 
Main Canal cluster in Rajasthan under M-CADWM schem e, the National Programme for Modernisation of 
Command Area Development and Water Management will be designed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 755 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 23, 2026 
 
STATUS OF PROJECTS UNDER AMRUT 2.0 IN RAJASTHAN 
 
NO. 755 SHRI HANUMAN BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether it has come to the notice of the Government that several 
projects relating to drinking water supply, sewerage, rejuvenation of 
water bodies and green space development sanctioned under AMRUT 
2.0 in various Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) of Rajasthan have not been 
completed within the stipulated time and if so, the reasons therefor; 
 
(b)  the details of the Central assistance sanctioned, released, utilised 
and currently pending for Rajasthan under the said mission, year and 
ULB-wise; and 
 
(c)  whether the Government is aware that citizens are facing severe 
inconvenience due to excessive delay in works related to drinking 
water pipelines, sewerage networks and road excavations in many 
cities of Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof along with the action 
taken to investigate the causes of these delays and fix the 
accountability of the concerned agencies? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (c): Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 
(AMRUT) 2.0, States/ Union T erritories are empowered to select, 
appraise, prioritise and implement the projects. Under AMRUT 2.0, t he 
State of Rajasthan has taken up 363 projects worth ₹ 11,560.07 crore 
(including operation and maintenance cost) , which includes C entral 
Assistance (CA) of ₹ 3,552 crore. The approved projects include 178 
water supply projects worth ₹5099.47 crore, 48 sewerage and septage 
management projects  worth ₹5950.85 crore, 134 water body 
rejuvenation projects worth ₹505.41 crore and 3 parks and green space 
projects worth ₹4.33 crore.  
…2/- 

-2- 
  
Central share of funds under AMRUT 2.0 are released to the States/ UTs 
and not Urban Local Body  (ULB)-wise. The State further distribute the 
funds to the ULBs as per progress of the projects. Up to the Financial 
Year (FY) 2025–26, CA amounting to ₹745.12 crore was released for 
AMRUT 2.0 projects to the State of Rajasthan. During the current year 
(FY 2026-27), Mother Sanction for ₹250 crore has been released for 
projects of which ₹104.44 crore has been utilised as on 20.07.2026.   
  
The projects under AMRUT 2.0 are implemented by the States/ UTs. The 
State has informed that 109 water supply projects of ₹1428.90 crore, 42 
sewerage and septage management projects of ₹4656.80 crore and 129 
water body rejuvenation projects of ₹ 443.86 crore have been awarded. 
As informed by the State, there have been some issues faced during the 
execution of projects such as delay in allotment of land/ area due to 
Court Cases/ local public hinderances; delay in receiving permission from 
various departments as Forest/ National Highway Authority of India 
(NHAI)/ Railway/ Public Works Department (PWD) etc.; delay in execution 
due to imposition of Graded Response Action Plan ( GRAP) in National 
Capital Region (NCR) cities; ban on construction work by the High Court, 
etc.  
 
The State Government has also informed that it is aware of the 
temporary inconvenience during the execution of works, including road 
excavation. The progress of these works is regularly reviewed, and 
necessary efforts have been made to remove the hindrances affecting 
their execution. The concerned agencies have been directed to expedite 
the works and restore the roads after completion.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 756 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 23/07/2026 
  
DISPOSAL OF CASES UNDER FOREST RIGHTS ACT, 2006 
  
756.  SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE:  
         DR. FAGGAN SINGH KULASTE:  
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has maintained any data regarding the number of Scheduled 
Tribe (ST) individuals and forest-dwelling tribal families claiming rights over forest land 
under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest 
Rights) Act, 2006, if so, the details thereof, State-wise including Scheduled areas of Madhya 
Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and other tribal dominated States;  
  
(b) the total number of individual and community forest rights claims received, approved, 
rejected and pending under the said Act during the last five years, State-wise;  
  
(c) whether the Government has assessed the reasons for the large number of rejected and 
pending claims in various States, if so, the details thereof along with the corrective measures 
taken by the Government;  
  
(d) whether the Government has formulated any special action plan to protect the forest 
rights of tribal communities, empower Gram Sabha and make their rights over minor forest 
produce and forest resources effective; and  
  
(e) the steps taken by the Government, in coordination with the State Governments to ensure 
time-bound recognition of eligible forest land rights of tribal communities and other 
traditional forest dwellers, including financial and technical assistance provided to the States 
for effective implementation of the Act? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGA DAS UIKEY) 
 
(a):  As per the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of 
Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (in short FRA) and Rules made thereunder, State Governments and 
UT Administrations are responsible for implementation of various provisions of the Act 
while the Ministry of Tribal compiles Monthly Progress Report received from the 
States/UTs. FRA is being implemented in 20 States and 1 UT. As per the latest information 

reported by States and collated under MPR as on 30.06.2026, a total of 54,01,561 claims 
have been filed by Forest Dwelling Scheduled Tribes (FDSTs) and Other Traditional Forest 
Dwellers (OTFDs), out of which 25,42,359 claims have been approved (titles distributed), 
18,13,232 claims have been rejected. The state wise status including details of Madhya 
Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and other tribal dominated states (where FRA is being 
implemented) is at Annexure.  
(b): As per reports submitted by States/UT, during the last five years period, i.e. from 
30.06.2021 to 30.06.2026, a total of 11,36,602 claims have been filed, 5,41,731 Claims have 
been approved (Titles Distributed), 29,524 claims have been rejected and 5,65,347 claims 
are pending for decision. Further, the details of number of claims (individual and 
community) received, the number of claims approved (Title distributed), Claims rejected, 
Claims disposed off during the last five years, month- wise and State/UT-wise are available 
at this Ministry’s website- on FRA- MPR-  https://tribal.nic.in/FRA.aspx. 
  
(c):    As per reports submitted by States/UT, as on 30.06.2026 a total of 18,13,232 claims 
(33.57% of total claims filed) have been rejected. Based on the information received from 
some of the State Governments, the major reasons for the rejection of claims are - claimed 
land not occupied before 13th December 2005, duplicate claims filed on the same land, 
claims on Non-Forest Land, lack of evidence, etc. Further, a total of 10,45,970 claims 
(19.36% of total claims filed) are pending for decision. It has been observed that the major 
reasons for pending claims are procedural delays in verification and disposal of claims at 
the Gram Sabha, Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) and District Level Committee 
(DLC) stages. State Government of Karnataka has informed that 88.7% of their pending 
claims are pending at SDLC level due to lack of public representation in SDLCs. States have 
been encouraged to fast-track the processing and disposal of pending claims in multiple 
national level consultation/ meetings/ workshops with States/ UTs, which are held from time 
to time.  
(d):   Ministry provides financial support to State Governments under the Dharti Aaba 
Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA) scheme for strengthening Gram Sabhas and 
Community Forest Resource Management Committees (CFRMCs), including support for 
constitution and functioning of CFRMCs, preparation and implementation of community-
led forest management plans, mapping of potential areas under FRA and support for 
preparation and execution of CFR Management Plans. 
  
(e):   The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, being the Nodal Ministry for administering the 
legislative matters of FRA, exhorts all State Governments to abide by the provisions 
contained in FRA and ensure that all eligible claimants are provided the rights which are 
due to them. Further, this Ministry provides financial assistance for the mapping of potential 
forest area, which can help state nodal departments for prioritizing and planning of FRA 
implementation. 
  
  
  

Annexure  
Annexure referred to in reply to part (a) of Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 756 
regarding “Disposal of Cases under Forest Rights Act, 2006” to be answered on 
23.07.2026.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.757 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 23rd July, 2026 
 
IMPACT OF WEST ASIA CONFLICT ON LPG SUPPLY AND PRICES 
 
757. SHRI ESWARASAMY K : 
   
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state 
  
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the ongoing conflict in West Asia on 
country's imports of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), including disruptions in shipping 
routes, freight costs and supply chains, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government has reduced the number of subsidised LPG cylinders provided 
under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) and if so, the reasons and rationale 
therefor;  
 
(c) the extent to which international LPG prices, freight charges and insurance costs have 
increased due to the conflict and its likely impact on domestic LPG prices; and 
 
(d) the measures taken or proposed by the Government to ensure uninterrupted availability of 
LPG across the country, including maintenance of strategic reserves, diversification of 
import sources and strengthening of supply logistics? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛमंũी  
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) Government remains committed to ensure uninterrupted supply of LPG in the country, 
including through imports. Diversification of LPG imports is being pursued to ensure supply security 
and mitigate risks arising from regional disruptions or geopolitical events. The number of LPG sourcing 
countries has increased from 10 to 15 countries and LPG is now sourced from a diversified pool of 
suppliers across countries in different regions of the world. As part of this strategy, PSU OMCs have 
concluded contracts for the import of ~2.2 Million Metric Ton (MMT) of US-origin LPG, covering nearly 
10% of the country’s total LPG import requirement. This marks a significant step in strengthening India’s 
energy resilience by establishing a reliable alternate LPG supply source outside the traditional Gulf 
region. 
 
 
To strengthen energy security and reduce supply risks, Government continuously monitors and 
assesses the threats, which can lead to potential supply disruptions of LPG. Public Sector Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs) also continuously monitor international shipping, freight, supply 

conditions, and undertake appropriate procurement and logistics management measures to ensure 
uninterrupted LPG availability across the country. Despite volatility in global energy markets, there has 
been no major disruption in domestic LPG supplies. 
 
(b) to (d) The Government remains committed to providing affordable clean cooking fuel to PMUY 
households while improving subsidy targeting. Based on LPG consumption trends of PMUY household 
in FY 2025–26, the annual subsidised refill limit has been revised from 9 to 4 cylinders, while retaining 
the subsidy at ₹300 per cylinder. 
 
Prices of LPG in the country are linked to its prices in the international market. Government continues to 
modulate the effective price to consumer for domestic LPG. 
 
While the average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for LPG pricing) was US$ 796/MT (excluding 
premium) in June 2026, the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder went 
upto Rs. 1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder. However, the Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being 
maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg cylinder. For PMUY consumers, the effective price is Rs. 642 per 
cylinder in July 2026 after a targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder.  
 
10.58 crore PMUY households continue to receive subsidy of ₹300 per cylinder in the form of direct 
benefit. The revised framework aims to balance support for vulnerable households with better targeting, 
fiscal prudence, and sustained adoption of clean cooking fuel. 
 
Prior to the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East in February 2026, India imported about 60 percent of 
its LPG consumption, out of which about 90 percent was transiting through the Strait of Hormuz. To tide 
over the crisis, Government has undertaken a series of proactive measures to ensure stability in LPG 
supplies post the outbreak of the conflict. These include rapid increase in domestic production of LPG, 
prioritization of domestic LPG consumption, diversification of import sources, dynamic stock 
management, and inter-regional & sectoral allocation to address localized shortages. 
 
The Government has also implemented several rationalisation measures on both the supply and demand 
side, including enhancing refinery production, increasing the booking interval to 25 days in urban areas 
and up to 45 days in rural areas and prioritising sectors for supply. 
 
Commercial LPG supplies were regulated in line with the prevailing crisis situation; in initial days in 
coordination with state governments and other stakeholders. These have been progressively relaxed. 
Government has now removed all sectoral restrictions on the supply of Non-Domestic Packed LPG and 
restored supplies to the levels prevailing prior to the West Asia crisis. Further, the supply of bulk LPG, 
which had been suspended at the onset of the crisis, has been relaxed by 50% of the pre-crisis 
consumption levels providing significant relief to commercial and industrial consumers.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 758 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
WITHDRAWAL OF NOMINEE FROM CDSE COMMITTEE 
758.  Adv DEAN KURIAKOSE: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the current stand of the National Dam Safety Authority with regard to the withdrawal of the nominee of 
the State Government of Kerala from the Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation (CDSE) Committee; 
(b) the reasons for the unilateral withdrawal of the nominee of the State Government of Kerala from the 
CDSE Committee; 
(c) whether the Government is considering to include the nominee of the State Government of Kerala in the 
CDSE Committee again; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (d)   In pursuance of the provisions of the Dam Safety Act, 2021 and the regulations framed thereunder, 
the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA) constituted an Independent Panel of Experts (IPoE) comprising 
five members for carrying out the Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation (CDSE) of the Mullaperiyar Dam, 
vide Office Memorandum dated 06th January, 2026. 
Subsequently, one of the members of the IPoE, who had been nominated by the State Government of 
Kerala, expressed his inability to continue as a member of the Panel due to personal reasons. In order to 
ensure the uninterrupted continuation of the CDSE process and to maintain the requisite strength and expertise 
of the Panel, the NDSA nominated another expert in his place. 
The replacement was necessitated solely on account of the concerned expert's unavailability and was 
undertaken in the interest of ensuring the timely completion of the dam's CDSE.  As the CDSE is a statutory 
exercise mandated under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, with a prescribed timeline for completion by December 
2026, the replacement was made to avoid any disruption or delay in the evaluation process and to ensure 
compliance with the statutory timeline. 
Further, responding to a request from the Government of Kerala, the NDSA wrote to the State on 25th 
June 2026 to nominate an independent expert to represent Kerala on the Mullaperiyar Dam CDSE's IPoE.

Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:

various Central schemes during the last five years, State-wise; 
(b)  the funds allocated, released and utilized for these schemes; and 
(c)  the reasons for delay in completion of pending projects?

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c): In order to promote and ensure overall development of Food Processing Industries, 
Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been incentivizing setting up/ expansion 
of related infrastructure, through its two Central Sector Schemes viz. Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing 
Industry (PLISFPI) and a Centrally sponsored PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing 
Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme across the country.  
The details of approved and operational/ completed projects under schemes of MoFPI 
from 2021-22 to 2025-26 is placed at Annexure-I. Year-wise total allocation & funds utilized 
under PMKSY, PLISFPI & PMFME from 2021-22 to 2025-26 across the country are given at 
Annexure-II. 
Delay in implementation of the food processing projects are due to various factors, such 
as the non-receipt of statutory clearances from the respective Agencies including the Revenue 
Authority, Town Planning, Electricity Authority, Water Authority, Pollution Control Board, 
Licensing Authority, etc. MoFPI has taken various measures for timely implementation of the 
projects, which include (i) Dashboard for monitoring the progress of the projects; (ii) 
Regularly review with the promoters to help remove bottlenecks in implementation; (iii) 
Assessing the progress of projects through site visits (including virtual visits) to prevent 
delays in their completion; (iv) Issues taken up with the Banks/ Financial Institutions to 
expedite sanction and disbursement of term loan to the projects; (v) Penal provisions on the 
promotors in case of delayed completion of projects .

MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 760 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
INSTALLATION OF DIGITAL FLOW METERS FOR GROUNDWATER EXTRACTION 
760. Shri ARUN BHARTI: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the new guidelines providing for mandat ory installation of digital flow meters for groundw ater 
extraction have come into effect from April, 2026 and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of industrial units that have succes sfully integrated their telemetry data with the Cen tral 
Ground Water Board pursuant to the said guidelines; 
(c) the mechanism for assessment and collection of Water Restoration Charges from entities found to be over-
exploiting local aquifers; 
(d) the details of applications for renewal of Grou ndwater No-Objection Certificates (NOCs) rejected d uring 
the current month due to inadequate rainwater harvesting structures; 
(e) the steps taken to prevent the illegal commerci al sale of groundwater by private tankers in water- stressed 
metropolitan cities; and 
(f) the total revenue generated through environmental compensation imposed on groundwater violators during 
the current financial quarter? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) & (b)    No new guideline has been notified in April ,2026 for mandatory installation of digital flow meters 
for groundwater extraction. However, existing guidelines for regulation and control of groundwater ext raction 
has been notified by the Ministry of Jal Shakti vid e S.O. 3289(E) dated 24.09.2020, as amended vide S. O. 
1509(E) dated 29.03.2023 prescribes installation of  digital flow meters for groundwater abstraction st ructures 
as per extant  guidelines. Under the prevailing reg ulatory framework, all project proponents granted N OCs by 
the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) are requi red to provide the credentials of their telemetry 
systems within 30 days from the date of issuance of the NOC. 
(c)  Water abstraction charges are levied in accordance  with the Guidelines notified vide S.O. 3289(E) dat ed 
24.09.2020, as amended vide S.O. 1509(E) dated 29.03.2023. The applicable charges are determined based on 
the category of the assessment unit, quantum of gro undwater extraction and the type of project, viz. 
infrastructure, industry or mining. The charges are  deposited by the project proponents through the 
Bharatkosh portal. 

2 
 
(d)   No application for  No Objection Certificates (NO Cs) renewal was rejected by CGWA during the current  
month due to inadequate rainwater harvesting structures. 
(e)   Under the prevailing regulatory framework, all bulk water suppliers extracting groundwater and supplying 
it through private tankers are required to obtain a  No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Central Gr ound 
Water Authority (CGWA) or concerned States/UT which ever is applicable  . Such bulk water suppliers are  
also required to pay groundwater abstraction charge s at the prescribed rates. Extraction of groundwate r for 
commercial use without a valid NOC is to be treated  as unauthorized and the defaulting entities are li able to 
pay Environmental Compensation for the quantity of groundwater extracted. Further, all tankers supplyi ng 
groundwater from such bulk water suppliers are requ ired to be equipped with a GPS-based system for 
monitoring their movement and area of operation.

extraction during the current financial quarter (April to June 2026) which is approx.Rs. 4 Cr  .

MINISTRY OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 761 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 23.07.2026 
 
EXPORT PROMOTION MISSION 
 
761.  SHRI EATALA RAJENDER: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has launched a comprehensive series of support measures for 
exporters, particularly focusing on Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and first -time 
exporters, through a Rupees 25,060 crore Export Promotion Mission (EPM) for the period 2025-2031 
with key initiatives that include the Market Access Support (MAS) scheme, increased credit 
guarantees and specialized aid for sectors affected by global trade disruptions; and 
 
 
(b)  if so, the details and the present status thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) and (b):  The Union Cabinet approved the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on 12th November 
2025 with the objective of strengthening India’s export competitiveness and providing targeted 
support to exporters in global markets, with a particular focus on Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs). The Mission operates through two integrated sub-schemes: 
 
a. Niryat Protsahan focuses on improving access to affordable trade finance for MSMEs through 
a range of instruments such as interest subvention, export factoring, credit guarantee and credit 
enhancement support for diversification into new markets. 
 
b. Niryat Disha focuses on non -financial enablers that enhance market readiness and 
competitiveness, including export quality and compliance support, assistance for international 
branding, packaging, and participation in trade fairs, export warehousing and logistics, inland 
transport reimbursements, and trade intelligence and capacity-building initiatives. 
 
EPM is anchored in a collaborative framework involving the Department of Commerce,  
Ministry of MSME, Ministry of Finance, and other key stakeholders, including Financial  
Institutions, Export Promotion Councils, Commodity Boards, industry associations, and  
state governments.

PNG NETWORK IN JHUNJHUNU 
 
†763. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether a comprehensive Piped Natural Gas (PNG) network is still not available for common 
citizens, commercial establishments and industries in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan despite the 
district having been included in the City Gas Distribution (CGD) network;  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for the delay in the development of the domestic 
and commercial PNG network in Jhunjhunu district along with the current progress of the project, 
sanctioned works and achievements made so far;  
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to introduce any scheme for the expeditious expansion of the 
network to provide PNG in all major cities and towns of Jhunjhunu district;  
 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the estimated timeline for implementation of the project along 
with the funds sanctioned and utilised so far, the results achieved therefrom and the proposed 
financial provisions and targets for the coming years, year-wise; and  
 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी) 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (e): Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections is part of the development of City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other 
facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and industrial units. This is being carried 
out by entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).  
Jhunjhunu District is a part of Jhunjhunu, Sikar and Nagaur districts Geographical Area (GA) 
authorized to Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL). IOCL has informed that a City Gate Station 
(CGS) has been established in Jhunjhunu for ensuring uninterrupted gas supply in the district. No 
funds are sanctioned or allocated by Government for implementation of the CGD projects. The 
investment is made by the authorized CGD entity in accordance with the authorization granted by 
PNGRB and the approved project plan. 

As on 31.05.2026, the authorized CGD entity has provided 3,307 PNG (Domestic) Connections and 
laid 214 Inch-KM of pipeline in the Jhunjhunu district. No Commercial or Industrial PNG 
connections have been released so far. 
Government have taken various steps to facilitate expeditious expansion of CGD network across the 
country including in Jhunjhunu district which, inter-alia, includes allocating domestic gas on priority 
basis to CNG (T)/ PNG(D); diverting domestic gas from non-priority sectors to meet the requirement 
for CNG (T)/PNG(D) sector, expansion of CGD network, grant of Public Utility Status to CGD 
projects, notification for supply of domestic gas through available mode (including cascade mode) 
for CNG(T)/ PNG(D) purpose, allocating domestic natural gas for CNG (T) and PNG (D) segments 
on a two-quarter advance basis, expansion of National Gas Grid Pipeline, setting up of Liquefied 
Natural Gas (LNG) Terminals, Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) 
initiatives to promote Bio-CNG, etc. 
The Government of Rajasthan has also rationalised VAT on domestic natural gas to 7.5% and 
notified a State CGD Policy to facilitate faster rollout of CGD infrastructure. 
Further, the Government has notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across 
the country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way 
(RoW) and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of delays, 
and prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also addresses access 
issues in residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time-bound permissions, 
thereby removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying.

MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 764 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF UDAN SCHEME  
764.    SHRI DILESHWAR KAMAIT                    
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has met its target of operationalising hundred 
unserved or underserved airports by early 2026 and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the roadmap and targets fixed for the next phase of expansion of airports under 
UDAN Scheme to unserved and underserved regions including the timelines and 
proposed locations; 
(c) the manner in which the increased budgetary allocation under the UDAN 
Scheme for the Financial Year 2026 -27 would be utilised to enhance last -mile 
connectivity in the North-Eastern Region; and 
(d) whether the Government has finalised the Seaplane Viability Gap Funding 
(VGF) Scheme to promote tourism in island territories and coastal regions and if 
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a)  As on 20.07.2026, a total of 679 RCS routes connecting 95 unserved and 
underserved airports, including 17 heliports and 02 water aerodromes, have been 
operationalised across the country under the UDAN Scheme.  
 
(b) & (c) The next phase of the UDAN Scheme was launched on 04.07.2026 to 
promote regional air connectivity in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and remote regions 
across the country, targeting 120 new destinations and 4 crore passengers over the 
next 10 years. The Scheme is being implemented from FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36 
with an outlay of Rs 28,840 crore, including ;Rs. 12,159 crore for Aerodrome 

development and Rs3,661 crore for development of 200 heliports in Hilly, North -
Eastern and Aspirational (HINER) States/districts. 
The Scheme provides a Challenge Mode framework under which State 
Governments may nominate airstrips for development. Proposals are evaluated 
based on availability of land, infrastructure readiness, technical and operational 
feasibility, traffic po tential, statutory clearances and su pport of the State 
Governments. 
 
 (d) In the Union Budget 2025 -26, it was announced that, to enhance last -mile and 
remote connectivity and promote tourism, the Government would incentivise 
indigenisation of seaplane manufacturing and introduce a Seaplane Viability Gap 
Funding (VGF) Scheme to support seaplane operations. The Scheme is presently at 
the formulation stage.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
  
FOOD PROCESSING INFRASTRUCTURE IN EASTERN INDIA 
  
765.  SHRI SUDHAKAR SINGH: 
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the details of mega food parks, cold chain projects and agro-processing clusters set up 
or approved by the Union Government in the country during the last three years; 
(b)  whether the Government has assessed the availability and development status of food 
processing infrastructure in the States of Eastern India, including Bihar and if so, 
whether any regional imbalance has been observed in these States compared to other 
regions and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c)  the schemes or concrete initiatives being undertaken by the Ministry to promote value 
addition of agricultural products, incentives for farmer producer organizations and 
rural employment generation in backward and agrarian regions.? 
   
ANSWER   
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
  
(a): The details of cold chain projects and agro-processing clusters sanctioned under 
PMKSY across the country over the last three years are provided in the Annexure. The Mega 
Food Park (MFP) scheme has been discontinued with effect from 01.04.2021. 
(b): The Ministry has undertaken an assessment of the infrastructure and logistics 
requirements of the food processing sector through the study titled "Assessment of the 
Infrastructure and Logistics Requirements of India's Food Processing Sector", 2025. The study 
evaluates the status of key infrastructure required for the sector, encompassing cold chain, 
warehousing, transportation, and logistics, and identifies major infrastructure gaps that require 
investment to support the sector's growth. However, the study does not detail any regional 
imbalance in food processing infrastructure, specifically with regard to the Eastern States, 
including Bihar, as compared to other regions. 
 (c): MoFPI is actively engaged in strengthening and promoting food processing and its 
related infrastructure throughout the country, operating through its Central Sector schemes—
namely the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) and the Production Linked 
Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)—alongside the Centrally sponsored 
PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme. All of these are 

demand-driven initiatives, expressly designed to create modern food processing infrastructure 
and establish efficient supply chain management that spans from the farm gate right up to the 
retail outlet. In fulfilling these objectives, the schemes collectively work to secure better returns 
for farmers, generate substantial employment opportunities across the nation—including in 
backward and agrarian regions—reduce the wastage of agricultural produce, enhance overall 
productivity, and raise the level of processing. As a direct consequence, these efforts boost the 
rural economy and make a meaningful contribution to inclusive and balanced growth. 
To enhance Farmer-Producer linkages, the following special benefits in financial assistance are 
provided to FPO category applicants under PMKSY: 
i. Grants-in-aid in form of subsidy @ 50% of eligible project cost as compared to 35% in 
general / difficult areas and in case of Food Safety and Quality Assurance Infrastructure 
(FSQAI) scheme the subsidy/grant-in-aid is @70% as compared to 50% in General 
areas; 
ii. Lower Equity Contribution – 10% required as against 20% for others; 
iii. Lower minimum credit/loan requirement – 10% required as against 20% for others; 
and 
iv. Lower Net-worth requirement i.e. equal to grant-in-aid sought, in comparison to 1.5 
times for General Category applicant. 
  Under the Promotional Activities scheme of MoFPI, the Ministry has extended financial 
assistance to various eligible organizations for organizing 48 events — comprising seminars, 
workshops, conferences, exhibitions — across the country during 2025, with the objectives of 
promoting value addition of agricultural products, providing incentives for farmer producer 
organizations, and creating awareness among private sector stakeholders, including small and 
marginal farmers, about the various schemes offered by the Ministry.

development of tribal communities in the country;

Jharkhand; 
(c) the number of beneficiaries provided assistance under the scholarship and skill 
development schemes for tribal students; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering providing a special development package 
for education, health, and livelihood in the tribal-dominated areas of Palamu and 
Garhwa and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER

(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
 
(a): The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing various schemes for the educational, 
social and economic development of Scheduled Tribes across the country. These 
schemes aim to improve education, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, infrastructure and 
socio-economic conditions of Scheduled Tribes. These schemes are as under: 
i. Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students: The scheme is applicable to students 
who are studying in Classes IX –X.  Parental income from all sources should not 
be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for 
day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is given for a period of 10 
months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT 
Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States 
except North East and Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and 
Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing 
pattern is 100% Central share. 

ii. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to 
provide financial assistance to the 
Scheduled   Tribe   students   studying   at   post-matriculation or post-secondary 
levels to enable them to complete their education.  Parental income from all 
sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees 
charged by educational institutions are reimbursed subject to the limit fixed by 
the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of Rs.230 to 
Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is 
implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except NE and 
Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir 
where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central 
share. 
  National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for ST 
students:    This a Central Sector Schemes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal 
Affairs. The   scheme has two sub-Schemes, viz: 
iii. a National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students 
(earlier known as Top Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, 
Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the 
selected top-class Government and Non-Government Institutes in professional 
fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, 
Law etc. All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding 
Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are 
eligible to receive scholarship. This scheme is started from year 2007-
08.                                        b.National Fellowship Scheme for Higher 
Education of ST Students:  It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs to grant scholarship to meritorious ST students for 
pursuing Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. This scheme is started 
from year  2005-06. The total number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year 
will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% marks in Master Degree up to 
the age of 36 years are eligible to apply for fellowship under the Scheme. The 
value of fellowship is at par with UGC rates.  
iv. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students: It is a Central Sector Scheme 
of Ministry of Tribal Affairs under which scholarships are given to the 
meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students for pursuing higher education in top 
1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) Institutes/Universities abroad. This 
scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is implemented through the 
Indian Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Affairs. Twenty awards 

are given every year. ST students with annual family income not exceeding 
Rs.6.0 lakhs are eligible to apply for the Scholarship under the Scheme.  
v. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan: Hon'ble PM launched Dharti 
Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan             Hon'ble PM launched Dharti 
Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October, 2024. The 
Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries and 
aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social 
infrastructure like hostels, Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set 
up Van Dhan Vikas Kendras to provide livelihood opportunities benefiting more 
than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in 5 years. 
The Abhiyan has a total budgetary outlay of Rs.79,156 Cr (Central share: 
₹56,333 Cr and State share: ₹22,823 Cr) 
vi. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN): 
Government launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan 
(PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG communities 
residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities 
such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, 
health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of 
unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. 
These objectives are planned to be met through 11 interventions including 
Hostels and Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) implemented by 9-line Ministries. 
PM JANMAN has total budgetary outlay of Rs.24,104 Cr (Central share: ₹15336 
Cr and State share: ₹8768 Cr). 
vii. Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution: Under the Proviso to Article 
275(1) of Constitution, Grants are released to States, having ST population for 
raising the level of administration in Scheduled Areas and for the welfare of 
tribal people. This is a Special Area Programme and 100% grants are provided 
to States. Funds are released to the State Governments depending on the felt 
needs of ST population to bridge the gap in infrastructure activities in the fields 
of education, health, skill development, livelihood, drinking water, sanitation, 
etc. 
viii. Grant-in Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of 
Scheduled Tribes:  Under the scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary 
Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, the Ministry funds 
projects in the fields of education and health, covering residential schools, non-
residential schools, hostels, mobile dispensaries, ten or more bedded hospitals, 
livelihood, etc. 

ix. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): The Scheme provides quality 
residential education to Scheduled Tribe students in remote and tribal areas with 
the objective of enabling them to access quality education comparable to the best 
institutions in the country. The schools provide modern educational 
infrastructure along with facilities for holistic development of tribal students. 
x.  Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM): The Mission promotes 
sustainable livelihoods of Scheduled Tribes through value addition, 
entrepreneurship development, marketing support and strengthening of tribal 
producer organisations, with emphasis on value chains based on Minor Forest 
Produce and other tribal products. 
xi. Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events 
(TRI-ECE): The Scheme supports Tribal Research Institutes for research, 
documentation, capacity building, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, 
awareness generation, information dissemination and evidence-based policy 
support. 
xii. Monitoring, Evaluation, Survey and Social Audit (MESSA): The Scheme 
supports monitoring, evaluation, impact assessment, surveys and social audit of 
programmes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to strengthen 
evidence-based planning, policy formulation and effective implementation of 
tribal development initiatives. 
xiii. Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST): The Scheme is 
implemented through the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development 
Corporation (NSTFDC) to provide concessional venture capital assistance to 
Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs for establishment and expansion of income-
generating enterprises. 
xiv. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation 
(NSTFDC): under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is an apex organisation set up 
exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes implements various 
schemes for livelihood generation. NSTFDC extends concessional loans to the 
eligible Scheduled Tribe communities. 
    Some of the above schemes may be Centrally Sponsored and other may be Central 
Sector Schemes. 
  
(b): Government of India has approved 91 Eklavya Model Residential Schools 
(EMRSs) in the State of Jharkhand, out of which 51 EMRSs are functional as on 
30.06.2026. 

(c): Under the scholarship schemes of the Ministry, 7.66 lakh Scheduled Tribe students 
have been supported under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme, while 17.17 lakh ST 
students have benefitted under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. Further, under the 
National Fellowship for Higher Education of ST Students, 2,961 ST students have been 
awarded Ph.D. fellowships, while 8,571 ST students have been received scholarships 
for pursuing higher education (UG/PG etc.). 
 Under the livelihood interventions implemented through the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya 
Vikas Mission (PMJVM), 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) have been 
sanctioned, benefiting about 12.48 lakh tribal members.In addition, under the VDVK 
component of PM-JANMAN, 540 VDVKs have been sanctioned benefiting 46,042 
beneficiaries. Further, NSTFDC has disbursed concessional loans amounting to 
₹1,648.39 crore to 4,95,090 beneficiaries during the last five years for income 
generation, self-employment and livelihood activities. 
  
(d): The Government follows an area-based and need-based approach for development 
of tribal areas through its ongoing schemes. In Jharkhand, Palamu district is covered 
under the PM-JANMAN for development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups 
(PVTGs), while Garhwa district is covered under the DAJGUA for saturation of 
infrastructure and basic services in eligible tribal villages. Further, one Eklavya Model 
Residential School (EMRS) each has been approved in Palamu and Garhwa districts 
under Article 275(1) of the Constitution, and both the schools are functional. 
Accordingly, development interventions relating to education, health, livelihood and 
other basic amenities are being implemented through these ongoing schemes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 767 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
IMPACT OF PRIVATISATION ON AIRPORT SERVICES  
767.    SHRI KULDEEP INDORA                      
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the details of the airports operated under the Public -Private Partnership 
(PPP) model or through privatisation during the last five years alongwith the 
airports proposed for privatisation; 
(b) whether the Government has c onducted any independent assessment 
regarding the impact of privatisation on airport charges, the financial burden on 
passengers, service quality, regional connectivity and the interests of employees 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Governme nt is considering consulting all stakeholders and 
conducting an impact assessment prior to the privatisation of more airports and 
if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken to ensure affordable services for passengers and to 
safegaurds for the rig hts and job security of employees following airport 
privatisation? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): At present, 17 airports, viz. Delhi, Mumbai, Lucknow, Ahmedabad, 
Mangaluru, Jaipur, Guwahati, Thi ruvananthapuram, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, 
Cochin, Kannur, Durgapur, Mopa, Navi Mumbai, Noida (Jewar) and Nagpur 
are being operated under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode. Further, 
eleven brownfield airports of Airports Authority of India (AAI) compri sing five 
major airports, namely Amritsar, Varanasi, Bhubaneswar, Raipur and 
Tiruchirappalli clubbed/paired with six smaller airports have been identified for 
bringing under PPP. 
 
(b) & (c): PPP of airports has helped in attracting private investment, crea ting 
world-class airports, delivering efficient and quality services to the passengers, 

as also reflected in consistently higher service quality ratings of Delhi, Mumbai, 
Bangalore and Hyderabad airports. Revenue share received by AAI from its 
airports under PPP has helped in development of airports in Tier -Il & lll cities. 
A study has also been undertaken through IIM Bangalore to assess the impact of 
PPP in the Airport Sector and their performance. Further, the PPP process is 
undertaken in accordance with the extant policy and approval framework under 
which the proposals are examined and approved by the competent authorities at 
various stages. 
 
(d):  Tariff determination for major airports is carried out by the independent 
statutory regulator, the Airport s Economic Regulatory Authority of India 
(AERA), which ensures that aeronautical tariff, including User Development 
Fees (UDF) remain reasonable and reflective of efficient airport operations 
while balancing the interest of all stakeholders. On implementat ion of PPP at 
AAI airports, employees of AAI have choice to either remain with AAI or opt 
to join PPP partner as their employee.

LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 768 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 23rd July, 2026 
 
EXPANSION OF NATIONAL NATURAL GAS PIPELINE NETWORK AND NATURAL 
GAS GRID 
 
†768. SHRI BHUMARE SANDIPANRAO ASARAM: 
   SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL: 
   DR. SHIVAJI BANDAPPA KALGE: 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has expanded the National Natural Gas Pipeline Network to ensure 
extensive regional connectivity across the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise including the States of Maharashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh; 
(c) whether supply of natural gas improved in industries, houses and especially in underserved 
areas from expansion of distribution network under the National Natural Gas Grid 
Expansion Scheme, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the role of the expanded natural gas pipeline 
infrastructure in promoting the use of clean energy and reducing dependence on 
conventional fossil fuels, if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; and 
(e)  whether the Government has established a monitoring and accountability mechanism to 
ensure the timely completion and effective implementation of ongoing natural gas pipeline 
projects, if so, the details thereof State/UT-wise especially with respect to the States of 
Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी ) 
    
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) & (b) Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is the authority to grant 
authorization to various entities to Lay, build, operate and expand Natural Gas Pipelines 
(NGPL). As on March 2026, PNGRB has authorized approximately 33027 Km of common 
carrier natural gas pipeline across the country to create a National Gas Grid. All the States and 
Union Territories, except Ladakh, Andaman & Nicobar Island and Lakshwadeep are covered by 
Natural Gas Pipeline Network authorized by PNGRB.  
The details of the Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipeline network including Maharashtra and 
Madhya Pradesh, authorized by PNGRB, are enclosed as Annexure-I. 
(c) & (d) The operational Natural Gas Pipeline network has increased from 15,340 km in 
September 2014 to 27,905 km as on March 2026. This expanding pipeline network interlinks gas 
supply sources with demand centres and enables seamless transportation of natural gas across 

regions, including hitherto unserved and underserved areas, thereby strengthening national 
energy connectivity. 
The expansion of the natural gas pipeline grid has significantly improved access of natural gas 
for City Gas Distribution (CGD) networks, industries, power plants and households. As on 
31.05.2026, the number of PNG Domestic connections has registered a substantial increase from 
22 lakh in 2013-14 to approx 170 lakh currently. Furthermore, authorized entities have 
established 8,936 CNG stations and provided 22,256 Industrial and 52,143 Commercial 
connections to support the clean energy transition in their respective Geographical Areas. 
The expansion of the natural gas pipeline grid across the country has significantly increased 
adoption of natural gas which has played a crucial role in reducing India’s dependence on 
conventional fossil fuels like coal and crude oil. Consumption of Natural Gas in the country has 
increased from approx 138 Million Metric Standard Cubic Meters per Day (MMSCMD) in 2014 
to approx. 188 MMSCMD in 2025. With expanding pipeline and CGD network, use of CNG as 
transportation fuel in vehicles (due to its cost effectiveness and lower emissions) is increasing. 
This has correspondingly reduced the demand for petrol and diesel which are refined from crude 
oil. Similarly, industries previously dependent on furnace oil and diesel are also progressively 
shifting to natural gas (mainly in the form of piped natural gas).  
The State/UT-wise details of CNG stations and PNG connections are enclosed at Annexure-II. 
(e) To ensure timely completion and effective implementation of ongoing natural gas pipeline 
projects across the country (including the States of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh), 
Government continually reviews and coordinates with the concerned State Governments and 
executing agencies to resolve the challenges such as securing Right of Use (RoU) of land, 
obtaining forest and environmental permissions, obtaining approvals for crossings such as 
Rivers, Canals, Railways, National Highways, etc.   
 
National Single Window System (NSWS) has been launched on 22.09.2021 by Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry which 
provides single platform to enable the stakeholders in identification of the issues and obtaining 
of approvals and clearances needed. For development of pipelines and CGD infrastructure, 
entities may apply for clearances & approvals on NSWS portal. The Know Your Approvals 
(KYA) module includes guidance for 32 Central Departments and 35 States.  
 
Government has launched PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, an integrated plan which will 
address the missing gaps to ensure seamless movement of people, goods & services. It aims to 
enhance ease of living, ease of doing business, minimize disruptions and expedite completion of 
works with cost efficiencies.  
 
Recently, a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 has been issued under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across the 
country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way 
(RoW) and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of 
delays, and prohibiting imposition of unauthorised charges by public authorities. It also 
addresses access issues in residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time- 
bound permissions, thereby removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
 
MSMEs SHUT DOWN IN ANDHRA PRADESH  
 
770.     SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY : 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)   the total number of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Andhra Pradesh that have 
shut down since 2024, sector -wise and year -wise including its comparison to the national  closure rate 
during the same period; 
(b)   the estimated total employment lost in Andhra Pradesh due to these MSME shutdowns during 
the last two financial years;   
(c)  whether the Ministry has assessed the specific vulnerabilities of granite polishing units, 
aquaculture processors a nd handloom cooperatives in Anantapur and Kurnool districts of Andhra 
Pradesh and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)   whether the Ministry is considering any central relief package or a special Credit Guarantee Fund 
Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)-backed restructuring facility to support the State's 
distressed MSME sector and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER

Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that motorists are alleged to have been protesting and 
backlashing over reduced mileage, potential engine damage, and lack of fuel choice; and  
(b)  if so, the details thereof along with the action taken by the Government thereon? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) & (b)  :  The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile 
manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) 
and other technical institutions. 
  
Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as Brazil 
operating higher ethanol blends for decades. In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme 
commenced with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained around 
1.53% in 2013-14, it has since been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after creating the 
necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework. 
The Government has not received any widespread or substantiated complaints from vehicle 
manufacturers, automobile associations or consumer organisations regarding engine failure, fuel 
pump issues, corrosion, water contamination or other performance issues attributable to E20 fuel. 
The Government has, however, taken note of certain concerns raised in media and social media, 
which have been scientifically examined. 
Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile 
manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for 
use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 
validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel.  

The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale 
experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting 
retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). 
E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for 
over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars have been 
operating on these blends without any verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle 
breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer service data confirm that there is no 
abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 fuel. Manufacturers continue to 
honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing further confidence in its safety 
and reliability. 
A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore 
vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible, and reported no E20-linked corrosion, 
abnormal wear or reduction in component life. A leading 2-wheeler company has reported similar 
field experience. One OEM recently stated that data from 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles tracked 
over an extended period showed no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion. ARAI reaffirmed that 
vehicles undergo rigorous international-standard validation before reaching consumers. 
With regard to mileage, studies by Government agencies and automobile manufacturers indicate that 
fuel efficiency is influenced by several factors, including driving conditions, driving habits and 
vehicle maintenance. Any reduction in fuel economy in certain E10-designed vehicles is generally 
limited to about 3-5%, while E20 offers a higher-octane rating, superior anti-knock characteristics, 
cleaner combustion and smoother engine performance. 
According to SIAM and ARAI, E20 improves acceleration and ride quality while reducing carbon 
emissions. Ethanol's higher-octane number supports modern high-compression engines and its higher 
heat of vaporisation improves combustion efficiency. 
The transition to E20 has also delivered significant national benefits. The Ethanol Blended Petrol 
Programme has saved over ₹1.97 lakh crore in foreign exchange, substituted nearly 316 lakh metric 
tonnes of crude oil, reduced around 952 lakh metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions and transferred over 
₹1.66 lakh crore to farmers. 
Accordingly, the Government's assertion that "no widespread issues" have been reported is based not 
on isolated instances but on the cumulative evidence of over 25 years of phased implementation, 
extensive scientific validation, continuous field experience across crores of vehicles, manufacturer 
service records, stakeholder consultations, and ongoing quality monitoring. 
The Government examines claims circulated on social media in consultation with manufacturers and 
technical agencies. Many such claims have been found to be exaggerated, misleading or unsupported 
by technical evidence and no verified evidence of widespread engine damage due to ethanol blending 
has emerged. 
In accordance with the Government's policy for implementation of the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) 
Programme, Oil Marketing Companies have been directed to supply Ethanol Blended Motor Spirit 
containing up to 20% ethanol, conforming to the relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) 
specifications, across all States and Union Territories. 
Further, with effect from 1 April 2026, Ethanol Blended Motor Spirit with a minimum Research 
Octane Number (RON) of 95 has been notified under the relevant statutory provisions. 
The Government's policy is to progressively transition towards cleaner, more efficient and 
environmentally sustainable fuels in line with the National Policy on Biofuels and India's energy 
security and emission reduction objectives. 

Automobile manufacturers, component suppliers, SIAM, ARAI, testing agencies and Oil Marketing 
Companies were associated with every stage of the scientific evaluation and phased rollout of E20. 
E20 was rolled out only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, 
reasonable material compatibility and emissions performance. These studies also established that 
legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear due 
to E20. Had automobile manufacturers not been fully satisfied with the results, they would neither 
have validated E20 fuel for older vehicles nor honoured warranty obligations. 
Having been scientifically validated and accepted by the automobile industry after extensive testing, 
there is no proposal to revert to E0/E10 petrol. The objective of public policy is to move forward 
with a superior fuel, not return to an inferior standard. 
The transition to E20 has been phased, consultative and scientifically validated, following extensive 
consultations with automobile manufacturers, ARAI, SIAM, Oil Marketing Companies and other 
stakeholders. Material compatibility, engine durability, fuel systems, drivability, emissions and 
performance were comprehensively evaluated before rollout. 
Maintaining parallel nationwide supply chains for E0, E10 and E20 petrol across more than one lakh 
retail outlets would significantly increase logistics complexity, inventory and handling costs. Public 
policy must balance consumer convenience with energy security, environmental sustainability and 
farmer welfare. 
Once a cleaner and scientifically validated fuel has been adopted, the objective is to move forward 
with better technology, not revert to an inferior standard.

heat of vaporisation improves combustion efficiency.
