GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 846 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 23, 2026 
 
FUNDS ALLOCATED FOR UTTAR PRADESH UNDER PMAY-U 2.0 
 
 
NO. 846   MS IQRA CHOUDHARY:  
SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA:  
SHRI LALJI VERMA:  
MRS RUCHI VIRA:  
SHRI HARENDRA SINGH MALIK:  
SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA:   
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has any data regarding the actual 
expenditure against the budget allocated, houses sanctioned, 
under construction, completed and handed over to beneficiaries 
under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana- Urban (PMAY -U) 2.0 during 
2025-26 across t he country and if so, the details and the present 
status thereof, particularly for Uttar Pradesh in Kairana, Ambedkar 
Nagar, Moradabad, Muzaffarnagar and Aonla Lok Sabha 
Constituencies and in Etah and Kasganj districts; 
(b) whether it is true that the approved housing projects could not be 
completed on time in urban areas of Uttar Pradesh including 
Kairana, Ambedkar Nagar, Moradabad, Muzaffarnagar and Aonla 
Lok Sabha Constituencies and Etah and Kasganj districts due to 
lack of basic infrastructure, deficiencies in quality of construction 
and administrative delays and if so, the reasons therefor along with 
the corrective steps taken thereon; 
(c) whether the Government is aware that a large section of families 
living in slums, tenants, homeless urban youth and other poor 
eligible persons have been deprived of the benefits of the said 
yojana due to its stringent eligibility criteria and if so, the details 
thereof, particularly in Kairana, Ambedkar Nagar, Moradabad, 
Muzaffarnagar and Aonla Lok Sabha Constituencies and Etah and 
Kasganj districts of Uttar Pradesh; 
...2/- 

 
-2- 
(d) the scheme of the Government to develop industrial corridors or 
skill development centres near these housing projects to link urban 
youth with employment, especially in respect of Kairana, Ambedkar 
Nagar, Moradabad, Muzaffarnagar and Aonla Lok Sabha 
Constituencies and Etah and Kasganj districts; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to make any amendments to the 
eligibility criteria and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e) : Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been 
implementing Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) since 
25.06.2015 to provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic 
amenities to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. Based 
on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY-
U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 
‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for 
implementation in urban areas across the country to support 1 
crore additional eligible beneficiaries in next five years. PMAY -U 
2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led 
Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), 
Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme 
(ISS). The Scheme Guideli nes may be accessed at https://pmay -
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-
2.pdf. 
 
PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 are demand driven schemes. As per the 
guidelines, States/ Union Territories ( UTs) are responsible for 
identifying beneficiaries, planning and executing projects and 
allotting completed houses. Citizens can apply through the Unified 
Web Portal of PMAY -U 2.0, where States/UTs/Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs) verify applications at multiple levels based on eligibility 
criteria. After demand assessment and beneficiary validation, 
States/UTs prepare project proposals, which are approved by the 
...3/- 

-3- 
 
State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) and 
then submitted to the Ministry for sanction of Central Assistance 
by the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC). The 
Unified Web Portal for submitting the online applications can be 
accessed through https://pmay-urban.gov.in.  
 
The contours of PMAY-U 2.0 including eligibility criteria have been 
designed on the basis of learnings of PMAY-U scheme, global best 
practices/ benchmarks and outcomes of series of consultations 
with multiple stakeholders including States/UTs, Banks, Housi ng 
Finance Companies, Private Sector etc. There is no proposal for 
making any amendments in the eligibility criteria by the Ministry. 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States/UTs, a total of 
127.68 lakh houses including 16.20 lakh under PMAY -U 2.0 have 
been sanctioned by the Ministry, so far. Out of which, 121.03 lakh 
houses have been grounded and 99.07 lakh are completed/ 
delivered to the beneficiaries across the country as on 13.07.2026. 
A total of ₹2,12,483 crores of Central Assistance have been 
approved of which ₹1, 80,582 crores have been released to 
States/UTs based on the compliances submitted by them.  
A total of 17.60 lakh houses have been sanctioned in the State of 
Uttar Pradesh under PMAY -U, of which 17.55 lakh houses have 
been grounded and 17.18 lakh are completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries which is around 98% of the total sanction. Under 
PMAY-U 2.0, a total of 3.99 lakh houses have been sanctioned in 
the State, of which 2.86 lakh houses are grounded and 0.07 lakh 
are completed, so far. Further, the total sanctioning and 
completion of houses in the State is more than the National 
average under these schemes. A total of   ₹ 33,628.24 crores of 
Central Assistance has been sanctioned under PMAY-U and PMAY-
U 2.0, of which 30,248.01 crore have been released to the State of 
Uttar Pradesh.  
 
...4/- 
 

-4- 
 
The details of houses sanctioned, grounded and completed along 
with Central Assistance approved and released under PMAY -U 2.0 
since inception, during 2025- 26 and current financial year across 
the country including Uttar Pradesh are at Annexure. The progress 
of the scheme can also be accessed on the PMAY -U dashboard 
(https://dashboard.pmay-urban.gov.in). 
As per the Scheme Guidelines of PMAY -U and PMAY -U 2.0, the 
State/UT Governments are responsible for providing basic 
infrastructure for the houses constructed under the scheme. 
Further, as per the scheme guidelines, States/UTs are encouraged 
to ensure convergence of the scheme with various other Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme and Missions including DAY-NULM (Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana–National Urban Livelihoods Mission)  and other 
relevant schemes for provision of related infrastructure services  
including developing skill development centers near the housing 
projects to provide livelihood opportunities to the beneficiaries . 
States/UTs may also develop Skill Development Centres  in 
convergence with the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and its programmes, including Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) , near housing projects to 
enhance livelihood opportunities for beneficiaries.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 849

KRISHI UDAN SCHEME  
849.    SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR               
    
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the quantity and value of agricultural produce transported under the Krishi 
UDAN Scheme from Andhra Pradesh during the last five years, year -wise and 
commodity-wise; 
(b) the details of the domestic and international destinations to which such 
produce has been transported under the said Scheme; 
(c) the details of cargo handling, cold storage and other infrastructure created 
under the said Scheme in Andhra Pradesh, district-wise; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to increase the participat ion of farmers, 
Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and exporters from Andhra Pradesh 
under the said Scheme? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d) The development of cargo facilities is a continu ous process and 
depends on various factors such as airport development progress, increase in 
scheduled operations, handling capacity, growth in domestic cargo volumes and 
demand from airlines. The details of cargo handling infrastructure and the 
volume of perishable cargo handled (in MT) through air cargo terminals in the 
State of Andhra Pradesh are given in Annexure. 
 
The airlines initiate cargo operations based on their internal assessment of cargo 
potential, handling capabilities and overall commercial viability of operating 
from any airport. Consequently, the decision to operate on any route rests with 
the airlines. 
 
In addition, the Krishi Udan Scheme aims to ensure seamless, cost -effective, 
time-bound, air transportation and associated logistics for a ll Agri -produce 

originating regions of the country, so that it improves their value realisation. All 
perishable commodities such as horticulture, fishery, livestock and processed 
products are covered under the Scheme.  
 
Under the Scheme, in order to facil itate and incentivise movement of agri -
produce by air transportation, waiver of landing and parking charges is provided 
for Indian freighters and P2C (Passenger -to-Cargo) Aircraft by the Airports 
Authority of India (AAI) and the Ministry of Defence at sele cted airports. In 
addition, Route Navigation Facility Charges (RNFC) and Terminal 
Navigational Landing Charges (TNLC) are waived at such selected AAI 
airports. Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development 
Authority (APEDA) also organizes tra ining and capacity building programs in 
collaboration with concerned Ministries for its stakeholders to sensitize its 
members regarding Government Schemes including Krishi Udan. 
****** 
  

Annexure 
 
Cargo handling infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh 
 
i. Visakhapatnam Airport : Airports Authority of India Cargo  Logistics 
and Allied Services Company Limited (AAICLAS) has established 
International cargo facility  with valuable cargo storage area, Hazardous  
Cargo, etc. AAICLAS has also established  domestic air cargo handling 
facility which is operated  through Operations & Maintenance (O&M) 
agency and the facility has separate rooms for valuable cargo storage and 
hazardous cargo etc. 
ii. Vijayawada Airport: AAICLAS has established domestic air cargo 
terminal.

Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) provides margin 
money subsidy of up to thirty five per cent for establishing new non -farm micro enterprises and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(b)  the number of micro enterprises established under above programme in Ramanathapuram  Lok 
Saba Constituency in Tamil Nadu during the last three years, along with the margin money subsidy 
sanctioned and released, category-wise; 
(c)  the number of employment opportunities generated through PMEGP -supported enterprises in 
Ramanathapuram Lok Saba Constituency during the said period; 
(d)  whether the Government has received representations or complaints regarding delays in 
sanction of bank loans, release of margin money subsidy or rejection of PMEGP applications from 
beneficiaries in said constituency and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  the steps taken to improve credit flow, expedite subsidy release and facilitate timely assistance 
to aspiring entrepreneurs in Ramanathapuram Lok Saba Constituency under PMEGP? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a): Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit linked subsidy 
scheme being administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by the Khadi and Village 
Industries Commission (KVIC) to assist prospective entrepreneurs in setting up of  new micro 
enterprises in the non -farm sector, by providing financial assistance in the form of Margin Money 
(MM) subsidy on bank sanctioned loans for generation of sustainable employment opportunities. 
 
PMEGP assists General category beneficiaries with MM Subsidy of 25% and project cost in 
rural areas and 15% in urban areas. For beneficiaries belonging to spec ial categories i.e. SC, ST, 
OBC, minority, Women, Ex -servicemen, physically handicapped, transge nders, beneficiaries 
belonging to NER, Hill and border areas and Aspirational districts, the MM Subsidy is 35% in rural 
areas and 25% in urban areas.

sanction of bank loans, release of MM subsidy, or rejection of PMEGP applications. The Ministry of 
MSME, KVIC, and the concerned district level implementing agencies including financing banks 
address them in a timely and systematic manner by providing suitable replies to beneficiaries to 
ensure effective redressal of their concerns. 
 
(e): Steps taken to improve credit flow, expedite MM subsidy release and facilitate timely 
assistance to aspiring entrepreneurs throughout the country including in Ramanathapuram Lok Sabha 
Constituency under PMEGP include the following: 
i. A new PMEGP Portal 2.0 launched as an end -to-end digital platform with BHASHINI for

Mobile applications.

sector and from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 20 lakh for service sector. 
iii. As per RBI Master Directions on lending to MSMEs, no collateral security to be insisted by

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 851 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
GREENFIELD AIRPORT IN DHANBAD  
851.    SHRI DULU MAHATO                         
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has completed any official technical feasibility 
study for Dhanbad Airport, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor; 
(b) the reasons for not convening a joint stakeholders' meeting so far de spite 
repeated representations from public representatives and whether the 
Government proposes to prescribe any timeline in this regard and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government admits that the lack of air connectivity since 1987 
in this r egion is the result of administrative inaction affecting industrial 
development and pilgrims visiting ‘Shri Sammed Shikharji’ and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) the details of the action taken so far on the letters sent to the State 
Government and the alt ernative strategy of the Ministry for desired progress in 
this regard; and 
(e) the clear roadmap for the project and the time by which it is likely to be 
completed? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): As per Greenfield Airports (GFA) Policy, 2008, if any Airport 
developer including the State Government desires to develop a Greenfield 
airport, they are required to identify a suitable site and get the Pre -feasibility 
Study conducted and submit a p roposal to the Central Government for 'Site 
Clearance' followed by 'In-Principle' approval. 
 
On the request of State Government of Jharkhand, a Pre -feasibility study for 
development of a Greenfield airport at Baliapur (Dhanbad) was carried out by 
multi-disciplinary team of Airports Authority of India in 2017 and the report 
was submitted to State Government. 
 

Proposal seeking 'Site Clearance' under GFA Policy for establishment of a 
Greenfield Airport at Dhanbad has not been received. 
 
As per GFA Policy,  the responsibility for implementation of the Greenfield 
airport projects including land acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement, 
funding etc. lies with the concerned airport developer or the State Government, 
as the case may be. The timeline for comple tion of the airport projects depends 
upon several factors such as land acquisition, availability of mandatory 
clearances, financial closure etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †852 
ANSWERED ON 23/07/2026 
JAL JEEVAN MISSION IN RAJASTHAN 
 
†852 SMT. MANJU SHARMA: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) the salient features of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM); 
(b) the number of districts in Rajasthan including Jaipur covered under the said Mission; 
(c) the number of households provided with new tap water connections under the said Mission in 
Rajasthan including Jaipur; 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any survey regarding the acute shortage of drinking water 
in Jaipur and if so, the details thereof along with the steps t aken/being taken by the Government in 
this regard; and 
(e) whether the Government has sanctioned any funds to Rajasthan under the said Mission during the 
current year and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
(a) The Union Cabinet Cabinet has approved extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) up to 
December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing on 
structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector unde r JJM 2.0. The key features of JJM 
2.0 are as under: 
i.  The outlay of the mission has been increased from ₹ 3.60 lakh crore to ₹ 8.69 lakh crore with 
enhancement of total central assistance from ₹ 2.08 lakh crore of ₹ 3.59 lakh crore. 
ii. Under JJM 2.0 separate MoUs to be signed with States/UTs to ensure structural reforms, 
adherence to timelines, schemes sustainability and delivery of citizen-centric water services. 
iii. Comprehensive Implementation and Reform Plan (CIRP), a structured and integrated framework 
to be prepared by each State/UTs for effective planning and implementation of JJM 2.0.  
iv. A uniform national digital framework, namely  “Sujalam Bharat ”, has been instituted, under 
which every village shall be assigned a unique Sujal Gaon / Service Area ID, digital ly mapping 
the complete drinking water supply system from source to tap. 
v. Strategic convergence among various Departments at Government of India level for sustainable 
and long-term operation and maintenance of rural water supply infrastructure and scheme source 
sustenance has also been envisaged under JJM 2.0. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
vi. Ministry of Jal Shakti to issue detailed operational guidelines for JJM 2.0 with the approval of 
Hon’ble Minister of Jal Shakti. 
vii. The disbursement of central assistance shall be scheme-wise through SNA -SPARSH. 
viii. No new piped water supply schemes shall be taken up under JJM 2.0. However, in PM-JANMAN 
and DA -JGUA areas, a Committee with representatives from the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 
Ministry of Rural Development, and Ministry of Panchayati Raj, shall examine a nd approve the 
State Action Plans pertaining to such schemes as per extant guidelines.  
ix. Community mobilization will be strengthened through focused IEC and Behaviour Change 
Communication (BCC) activities. Under this, Jal Utsav will be organized with active  
participation of the community and Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) to promote 
activities such as leakage detection, improving water distribution efficiency, carrying out minor 
repairs, and better asset management. Further, Jal Arpan will be undertaken for the formal 
commissioning and handing over of completed water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats, 
ensuring community ownership and sustainable operation of the systems.   
(b) & (c) JJM 2.0 aims to facilitate the certification of all Gram Panch ayats as ‘Har Ghar Jal’, by 
provisioning tap water connection to all the 19.36 crore rural households across the country by 
December 2028, including all the districts in Rajasthan.  
At the start of the mission, only 11.74 lakh (10.90%) rural households wer e reported to have tap 
water connections in Rajasthan. So far, under JJM, more than 51.88 lakh additional rural households 
have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 19.07.2026, out of 1.07 crore rural 
households in the State, more than 63. 62 lakh (59.10%) households are reported to have tap water 
connections in their homes.  
Similarly, at the start of the mission, around 0.81 lakh (15.73%) rural households were reported to 
have tap water connections in Jaipur district of Rajasthan. So far, around 2.56 lakh rural households 
have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. Thus, as on 19.07.2026, out of 5.13 lakh 
rural households in the district, around 3.37 lakh (65.70%) households are reported to have tap water 
connections in their homes. The State/ UT, district & village -wise status of tap water connection in 
rural households etc. as reported by States/ UTs is in public domain and available on JJM dashboard 
at: https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx 
(d) Drinking Water bein g a state subject, it is States, who plan, design, approve and implement 
drinking water supply schemes. Government of India supplements the efforts of the States by 
providing technical and financial assistance under this mission. As informed by the State o f 
Rajasthan, surveys and assessments have been conducted in Jaipur to address the issue of drinking 
water shortage. These include groundwater and source assessments by the Central Ground Water 
Board and infrastructure and supply reviews by the State PHED, which have identified declining 
groundwater levels and heavy dependence on limited surface sources. State has further informed that 
based on these findings, the State government has taken steps such as augmentation of surface water 
supply (including streng thening of Bisalpur -based systems), expansion of bulk transmission and 
distribution networks, water quality monitoring, recharge measures and planning of sustainable 
drinking water solution to improve availability and sustainability of drinking water in Jaipur. 
(e) The State Government of Rajasthan has been tentatively allocated an amount of Rs.4503.18 crore 
for the FY 2026-27, of which mother sanction of amount Rs. 278.88 crore has been issued along with 
the reimbursement of amount Rs. 537.72 crore release d to the State on account of  additional 
expenditure incurred by the State between the phases of two Mission period.

Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  the salient features of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and the progress made thereunder since its 
launch;  
(b)  the number of registered beneficiaries under the Scheme, indicating the number of beneficiaries 
who have received Skill Upgradation Training, Toolkit Incentive and collateral -free credit State-wise 
and district-wise in Karnataka;  
(c)  the total amount of credit sanctioned and disbursed under the Scheme, State-wise, including for 
Shivamogga district in Karnataka;  
(d)  the initiatives undertaken to provide market access to beneficiaries through Government 
eMarketplace (GeM), e-commerce platforms, exhibitions, branding and quality certification; and  
(e)  the measures taken to increase enrolment, awareness and saturation of benefits among eligible 
artisans, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a):   PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched on 17.09.2023 to provide end -to-end holistic support 
to artisans and craftspeople of 18 traditional trades who work with their hands and tools. The scheme 
covers 18 trades, namely: Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal A rtisan, Tool Kit Maker, 
Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Footwear Artisan, Mason, 
Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor and 
Fishing Net Maker. 
 
Salient features of PM Vishwakarma: 
 
i.   Recognition: Recognition of artisans and craftspeople through PM Vishwakarma certificate and 
ID card. 
ii.  Skill Upgradation: Basic Training of 5-7 days and Advanced Training of 15 days or more, with 
a stipend of Rs. 500 per day and transport allowance of Rs 1000. 
iii. Toolkit Incentive: A toolkit incentive of upto Rs. 15,000 through e -vouchers after Basic Skill 
Training. 
iv.  Credit Support: Collateral free 'Enterprise Development Loans' of upto Rs. 3 lakh in two tranches 
of Rs. 1 lakh a nd Rs. 2 lakh with tenures of 18 months and 30 months, respectively, at a 
concessional rate of interest fixed at 5%, with Government of India subvention to the extent of 
8%. 
v.  Incentive for Digital Transaction: An amount of Re. 1 per eligible digital tra nsaction, upto 
maximum 100 eligible transactions monthly will be provided to the beneficiary for digital pay -
out or receipt.  
vi.  Marketing Support: Marketing support in the form of quality certification, branding, onboarding 
on e-commerce platforms such as GeM, advertising, publicity and other marketing activities to 
improve linkage to value chain. 
 
 
 

 
: 2 :

(GeM), Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) and reputed e-commerce platforms. More than

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 857 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
UPGRADATION OF CHENNAI INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT  
857.     THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN              
  
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Union Government has assessed the reasons for Chennai 
International Airport's declining passenger traffic and national ranking despite 
being one of India's oldest and busiest aviation hubs and if so, the detai ls 
thereof; 
(b) the steps taken to augment capacity, improve passenger amenities, 
modernise airside infrastructure and reduce runway congestion at Chennai 
International Airport during the last five years along with the funds spent and 
the present status of these works; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of airline route 
suspensions, limited slot availability and infrastructure constraints on Chennai's 
domestic and international connectivity and if so, the details thereof including 
the measures taken to restore the lost services; 
(d) the reasons for the delay in completing the ongoing integrated terminal and 
parallel taxiway projects and the revised timeline fixed therefor; and 
(e) the long -term strategy of the Government to ensure that Tamil Nadu's 
principal aviation gateway remains globally competitive and does not lose 
traffic and investments to other metropolitan airports due to inadequate 
infrastructure planning? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): There has been no decline in passenger traffic at Chennai International 
Airport and the airport has consistently retained its position as the fifth busiest 
airport in the country in terms of passenger traffic since FY 2022-23. 
 
(b): The Air ports Authority of India has undertaken the expansion and 
modernization of Chennai Airport in two phases at a total cost of Rs. 2467 

crore. Under Phase-I, a New Integrated Terminal Building has been constructed, 
increasing the airport's passenger handling capacity from 23 Million Passengers 
Per Annum (MPPA) to 30 MPPA. The terminal has been operational since 
08.07.2023. Phase -II involves the development of Terminal -3, which will 
enhance the airport's capacity to 35 MPPA. An expenditure of Rs. 1762.08 crore 
has been incurred on the project up to June 2026. Further, to enhance airside 
infrastructure and improve operational efficiency, AAI has completed various 
airside infrastructure works, including Rapid Exit Taxiways (RETs), taxi tracks, 
link taxiways etc. at a total cost of Rs. 236.75 crore during the last five years.  
 
(c): No limitation regarding availability of slots has been observed at Chennai 
airport and no request for slot allocation by any airline is pending with AAI. 
Since deregulation of the domes tic aviation sector in March 1994, airlines 
determine their aircraft deployment and route network based on operational and 
commercial viability. Accordingly, introduction of air services is at the 
discretion of the airlines. International air services are governed by the bilateral 
Air Services Agreements (ASAs) between India and the respective countries, 
commercial viability, passe nger demand, slot availability, operational 
feasibility, and other associated factors. 
 
(d): The modernization of Chennai Airpor t has faced delays primarily due to 
unforeseen natural calamities, including the COVID -19 pandemic, multiple 
cyclones, and unusually high rainfall. The revised timeline for completion of the 
project is December 2026. 
 
(e): AAI continuously upgrades and au gments infrastructure at Chennai 
International Airport to enhance operational efficiency, improve passenger 
experience and meet future traffic requirements.

NO. 862  SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE:  
SMT. SUPRIYA SULE:  
SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has recently undertaken large- scale 
programmes in some States under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban 
(PMAY-U) 2.0 for sanction of houses and Grih Pravesh of beneficiaries 
and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the number of beneficiaries in Maharashtra who have been 
sanctioned houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY-U) 
2.0 and the amount of Central assistance released to the State during 
each of the last three years;  
(c) the details of completed houses and beneficiaries who have 
undertaken Grih Pravesh in Maharashtra under Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) 2.0, district-wise;  
(d) whether the Government proposes to organise similar large- scale 
beneficiary outreach and housing distribution programmes in 
Maharashtra and if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) the measures taken to expedite approvals, release of funds and 
completion of affordable housing projects in Maharashtra to achieve the 
objective of "Housing for All" within the stipulated timeframe? 
 
 
 
 
 
…2/- 
 
 
 

-2- 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e): ‘Land’ and ‘Colonization’ are State subjects. Therefore, all 
schemes related to housing for their citizens are implemented by 
States/Union Territories (UTs) in their respective areas. However, Ministry 
of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) supplements the efforts of 
States/UTs by providing Central Assistance under Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) since June 25, 2015 to provide pucca houses to 
all eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY-U, 
MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for 
All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas 
across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible beneficiaries.  
PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led 
Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable 
Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).  
PMAY-U and PMAY -U 2.0 adopt  a demand driven approach wherein 
States/Union Territories (UTs) assess the requirement through their Urban 
Local Bodies (ULBs)/Implementing Agencies in their respective 
jurisdictions. Eligible citizens are also allowed to apply through Unified 
Web Portal of PMAY -U 2.0 with all details on the portal. States/UTs/ULBs 
validate the beneficiaries as per the eligibility criteria of the scheme 
guidelines and selection/scrutiny of beneficiary lists are done by the 
States/UTs. The Scheme Guidelines and Unified Web Portal for submitting 
the online applications can be accessed through https://pmay-urban.gov.in.  
Based on the demand survey and selection of beneficiaries, the project 
proposals are prepared and approved by the State Level Sanctioning and 
Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) headed by the Chief Secretary of 
States/UTs for further consideration of release of Central Assistance by 
the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC).   
…3/- 
 

-3- 
Central assistance under PMAY -U & PMAY-U 2.0 is released to States/UTs 
in three installments of 40%, 40% and 20%. The release of Central 
assistance is incumbent upon fulfillment of mandatory compliances by the 
concerned States/UTs as per operational guidelines and other instructions 
issued by Ministry of Finance. Due installment of Central assistance is 
released as soon as requisite compliances are achieved in sanctioned 
projects, to concerned State Government for transferring it along with 
matching state share to the identified beneficiaries for construction of 
houses under the scheme. 
Based on the project proposal submitted by State of Maharashtra, a total 
of 13.84 lakh houses including 1.98 lakh under PMAY -U 2.0 have been 
sanctioned by the Ministry, so far. Out of which 12.16 lakh houses have 
been grounded and 10.74 lakh are completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries. The total houses sanctioned under PMAY -U and PMAY-U 2.0 
and the amount of Central assistance released to the State during each of 
the last three years is at Annexure- I. The district wise details of the 
houses sanctioned, grounded and completed/delivered to the beneficiaries 
under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 in Maharashtra is at Annexure-II. 
The Ministry conducts regular review with the States/UTs on progress of 
the scheme including timely submission of compliances by States/UTs for 
subsequent release of Central Assistance and its utilization and expedite 
completion of sanctioned houses within the stipulated timeline. 
PMAY-U 2.0 supports States/UTs for formulation and implementation of 
‘Affordable Housing Policies’ to incentivize private sector participation 
through appropriate regulatory, fiscal and institutional measures to make 
the housing stock affordable in urban areas. The Scheme Guidelines can 
be accessed at https://pmay urban.gov.in. 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) advises all States/UTs 
including Maharashtra to conduct various outreach programmes/ 
campaigns for creating awareness. States/UTs are encouraged to organize 
awas mela, regional sanction- letter distribution camps and mass Grih 
Pravesh ceremonies , etc. to publicly celebrate the completion of homes 
while encouraging local community participation.  However, a database of 
such outreach activities is not maintained centrally.

53 (Old NH -6) Bhandara –Deori section in Maharashtra executed under

from the original concession agreement by not constructing four 
Vehicular Underpasses (VUPs) and about eight kilometres of the 
approved road length, if so, the details thereof;

crore became recoverable from the concessionaire by the National 
Highways Authority of India (NHAI), if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the NHAI failed  to initiate recovery proceedings for nearly 
ten years despite the contractual violations, thereby allegedly extending 
undue financial benefit to the concessionaire; and

officials held acco untable and  the corrective and punitive measures

Agreement. The financial and contractual implications of the de -scoped 
works were finalized under the Settlement Agreement dated 27.04.2022

Concessionaire.

7.944 km forest stretc h, was duly adjusted / set off against the 
settlement amount payable by NHAI.   
(c) to (d) The issues relating to Change of Scope, toll revenue 
compensation and other contractual claims / counter -claims of the NHAI 
have been resolved through Settlement Agr eement dated 27.04.2022 in

due legal process.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. - 869 
ANSWERED ON 23rd JULY, 2026 
 
IMPACT OF ETHANOL-BLENDED PETROL ON VEHICLES 
 
869.  MS. MAHUA MOITRA: 
 SHRI K RADHAKRISHNAN: 
 SHRI DHARMENDRA YADAV: 
   
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of complaints regarding poor  
vehicle performance,  reduced fuel efficiency, technical defects, 
engine, fuel system and other component -related damage and 
maintenance problems allegedly associated with the use of ethanol -
blended petrol, particularly in older vehicles and two -wheelers and if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted or commissione d any 
scientific, technical or other  assessment to examine the impact of 
ethanol-blended petrol on different categories of vehicles,  particularly 
older vehicles and two -wheelers, if so, the findings of  such studies 
thereof; 
(c) the number and nature of com plaints received during the last three  
years and the current year, State/UT-wise and year-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has issued or proposes to issue any 
safety standards, compatibility guidelines, advisories or directions to 
vehicle manufacturers and  Oil Marketing  Companies regarding the 
compatibility, quality and safe use of ethanol -blended petrol and if so,  
the details thereof; and 

(e) the steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to 
address consumer  grievances, safeguard vehicle owners from any 
adverse effects, ensure the quality and suitability  of ethanol -blended 
petrol supplied across the country and promote the use of ethanol -
compatible vehicles while providing adequate safeguards for existing 
vehicles? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) and (c) E19–E20 fuel has been in use for over two -and-a-half years. 
As per information received from Society of Indian Automobile 
Manufacturers (SIAM), no widespread issues of engine failure or 
vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending have been 
reported. Certain concerns relating to engine performance, mileage 
and vehicle wear have been arising largely through public commentary 
and social media discourse. 
(b) and (e) Yes, Government in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas has introduced the Etha nol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme by 
consultation with stakeholders, field trials and validation by expert 
agencies at each stage of blending escalation: 
i. Ethanol Blending Program is administered by the Government in 
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.   A Study for the 
evaluation of effects of E20 on BS -III, BS -IV and BS -VI E10 
(Gasoline) two -wheelers and four -wheelers was carried out 
jointly by Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Indian Institute 
of Petroleum (IIP) Dehradun, Society of Indian Automob ile 
Manufacturers (SIAM) and Automotive Research Association of 
India (ARAI). The exhaust emissions meet the respective norms 
(ie BS VI vehicles meet the BS VI emission norms when tested 
with E20). The studies have not shown any need to modify the 
car and two-wheeler engines. These studies confirmed that even 
legacy vehicles did not exhibit any significant variations in 

performance, nor do they show abnormal wear -and-tear when 
operated with E20 fuel. No issues were reported in parameters 
such as drivability , startability, metal compatibility, and plastic 
compatibility. Only in case of testing done on BS -III vehicles 
introduced from 1 st April, 2005 and manufactured prior to 2016, 
some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement, which 
can be easily manag ed during routine servicing regime of the 
vehicle. With regard to the concern of vehicle mileage due to the 
use of E20 fuel, Government, automobile manufacturers and 
vehicle/engine testing agencies have clarified that vehicle 
mileage is influenced by a hos t of factors beyond just fuel type. 
These include driving habits, maintenance practices such as oil 
changes and air filter cleanliness, tyre pressure and alignment, 
and even air conditioning load.  
ii. An Inter -Ministerial Committee (IMC), constituted on 26 
December 2020 under NITI Aayog, comprehensively examined 
vehicle compatibility and mileage/efficiency aspects of ethanol 
blending. This assessment was supported by research conducted 
by Indian Oil Cor poration Ltd. (IOCL), the Automotive Research 
Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile 
Manufacturers (SIAM). 
iii. The Committee's "Roadmap for Ethanol Blending in India 2020 -
25", released in June 2021, was prepared after extensive 
consultation with automobile manufacturers, oil companies and 
agricultural experts, and examined material compatibility, engine 
calibration, fuel systems, drivability, durability, emissions and 
fuel efficiency. The Committee’s report preceded the introduction 
of E-20 fuel.  
The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented 
through a phased, calibrated, scientifically validated and consultative 
approach.  
It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as 
Brazil operating higher eth anol blends for decades. In India, the 
Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme commenced with a pilot in 
2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained 

around 1.53% in 2013 -14, it has since been increased progressively in 
a calibrated manner after creating the necessary production capacity, 
infrastructure and regulatory framework. Before the introduction of 
E20, extensive laboratory studies, durability trials and field validation 
were undertaken covering engine durability, material compatibi lity, 
fuel systems, corrosion resistance, drivability, emissions, fuel 
economy and overall vehicle performance. 
As seen from the table, the progression has been gradual: 
Ethanol Supply Year Average Blending (%) 
  
2013-14 ~1.53 
2020-21 ~8.1 
2021-22 ~10 
2022-23 ~12 
2023-24 ~14.6 
2024-25 ~19.2 
2025-26 (Nov-June) 20 
   
(d) The Government in Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has 
notified Safety Standard (AIS 171) for various blends of ethanol with 
gasoline vide G.S.R 343 (E) dated 25th May 2021.

ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY 2026 
  
 DELAY IN CONSTRUCTION OF NATIONAL HIGHWAY-39 
  
870. DR. RAJESH MISHRA: 
           
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the number of National Highway projects in the country that have 
remained under construction and are yet to be completed during the 
last ten years; 
(b) the number of construction agencies with which contracts have 
been awarded so far for the construction of National Highway -39, which 
commenced during the year 2012-13; 
(c) the reasons for the non -completion of work or termination of 
contracts by the said construction agencies; 
(d) the original cost of the said project, the total expenditure incurred 
thereon so far and the estimated financial loss caused to the 
Government due to the delay in its completion; 
(e) the actio n taken or proposed to be taken against the defaulting 
agencies and the officers responsible for the delay in the execution of 
the project; 
(f) whether the project is presently being executed by the National 
Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and if so, th e revised timeline fixed 
for its completion; and 
(g) the specific steps taken by the Government to ensure that the 
project is completed within the revised timeline? 

 
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) 1,187 National Highway (NH) projects, construction of which 
commenced during last 10 years are at under construction stage 
without attaining project completion and excluding projects under 
consideration for termination / foreclosure.  
(b)  to (g) 3 different concessionaires were engaged in Financial Year 
(FY) 2011-12 for (i) Bameetha-Satna (ii) Satna to Bela and (iii) Sidhi to 
Singrauli section of NH -39 in the State of Madhya Pradesh on Design, 
Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer ( DBFOT) for which  Appointed 
Dates were declared in FY 2013-14.     
Concession agreements were terminated for all the above three 
works owing to persistent non -achievement of contractual milestones 
and continued non -performance by the concessionaires. Subsequently, 
works were re-awarded on EPC basis and 2-lane with paved shoulders / 
4-lane works have been completed for (i) Bameetha -Satna (ii) Satna to 
Bela section respectively in FY 2020-21. Further, contract for remaining 
work was again terminated for Sidhi - Singrauli section owing to poor 
performance of the contractor in FY 2020-21.  Subsequently, the work 
was again re -awarded in FY 2026 -27 and appointed date was declared 
on 09.05.2026 with scheduled date of completion on 08.05.2028.        
Total original sanctioned cost of these 3 projects w as Rs. 1,597 
crore and total expenditure incurred, so far, is Rs. 2,085 crore. 
The Government has put in place a framework using multiple 
mechanisms for monitoring project progress and contractor related 
issues. Regular review meetings are conducted at various levels with 
stakeholders to assess project progress and resolving the site related 
issues of land acquisition, material availability, clearances etc. All 
efforts are made to resolve all such pending issues, including 

contractor / concessionaire related issues, in close coordination with 
the State Governments and other stakeholders, to complete these 
projects. 
The Government  leverages the mechanism of review and 
resolution of bottlenecks/hindrances in ongoing projects, in active 
collaboration with the State Governments and other stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 871 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
  
FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRY HUB 
  
871. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the potential of developing Bijnor, a leading 
district in agriculture and sugarcane production with excellent road and rail 
connectivity, as a Food Processing Industry Hub and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is considering establishing a special Food 
Processing Zone/Mega Food Park in Bijnor to enhance value addition, storage and 
export of sugarcane, potato, fruits and other agricultural products and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether there is a proposal to develop cold chain, warehouse, testing 
laboratories, packaging and processing infrastructure for this purpose and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) the details of the proposed action plan, financial provisions and the timeline thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
(a) : In order to promote and ensure overall development of the food processing sector, Ministry 
of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) incentivizes entrepreneurs to establish related 
Industries through its two Central Sector Schemes namely Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA 
Yojana (PMKSY) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry 
(PLISFPI) and a centrally sponsored scheme namely PM Formalization of Micro Food 
Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme across the country including Bijnor district of Uttar 
Pradesh. 
In order to promote local industries, One District One Product (ODOP) approach under 
PMFME Scheme has been adopted to reap the benefit of scale in terms of procurement of 
inputs, availing common services and marketing of products. It provides the framework for 
value chain development and alignment of support infrastructure. Under PMFME Scheme, 
Jaggery has been identified as ODOP for Bijnor district. As on 30.06.2026, 290 micro food 
processing enterprises have been approved in Bijnor district, out of which 82 micro food 
processing enterprises are related to jaggery processing. 
  
(b) to (d) : MoFPI was implementing Mega Food Park (MFP) Scheme, a component scheme 
under PMKSY. The implementation of MFP scheme has been discontinued with effect from 
01.04.2021.  However, under various component schemes of PMKSY, MoFPI provides 

financial assistance for creation of cold chain facilities, processing infrastructure, packaging 
and quality testing laboratories across the country including Bijnor district of Uttar Pradesh.  
  
MoFPI does not set up food processing units on its own. However, it provides financial 
assistance in the form of grants-in-aid to eligible entrepreneurs for establishing related 
infrastructure, through its schemes as per related scheme guidelines across the country 
including Bijnor district of Uttar Pradesh. These schemes are demand driven and intended to 
support food processing infrastructure and value addition.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION  NO.  873 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
  
WIDENING OF NATIONAL HIGHWAY-730 
  
 †873. SHRI UTKARSH VERMA MADHUR: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that National 
Highway (NH) -730 and the Lakhimpur -Sitapur-Lucknow route 
witness severe daily traffic congestion in Lakhimpur city due to 
heavy vehicles and sugarcane crushing season of sugar mills; 
(b) if so, whether any proposal to construct a new ring road or an 
outer bypass to relieve Lakhimpur city from this traffic congestion 
is under consideration of the Government, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) th e current status of progress regarding the widening/4 -lane/2-
lane with paved shoulders) of various sections of National Highway -
730 connecting the India -Nepal International Border (Gauriphanta 
Border) and the timeline set for the completion of this strateg ically 
important route; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to take eco -friendly 
measures, such as the construction of elevated corridors or 
underpasses, to ensure the safety of wildlife on the highway passing 
through the Eco -Sensitive Zone of Dudhwa  National Park, if so, the 
details thereof? 
  
  
  

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to  (d)    The Government through this Ministry is primarily 
responsible for development and maintenance of National Highways 
(NHs). Development and maintenance of NHs is a continuous 
process. Works on NHs are accordingly taken up based on the 
traffic density , condition of road and synergy with PM Gati Shakti 
National Master Plan to keep the NHs in traffic worthy conditions.    
          NH - 730 starts from Pilibhit on NH -30 connecting Puranpur, 
and terminating at NH -27 near Salemgarh in the State of Uttar 
Pradesh and has a total length of about 568 km; about 497 km 
length of NH-730 has been developed to 2 Lane with paved shoulder 
configuration including the stretches adjoining Lakhimpur city; 
projects in about 67 km length of NH -730 are in various stages of 
progress for upgradation to 2 Lane with paved shoulder 
configuration including construction of bypasses, ROBs, flyovers, 
etc., and are targeted for completion in phased manner by 
06.11.2027. 
          The following works have been completed on NH 730 for 
easing traffic congestion in Lakhimpur city: - 
(i) Upgradation to 2 Lane with Paved shoulder from Khutar -
Lakhimpur section (Km 82.00 to 140.00); 
(ii) Construction of 1 ROB & 2 flyovers at the section from Km 
133+230 to Km 134+330, Km 134+550 to Km 135+650, K m 
136+200 to Km 137+800.  
          Detailed Project Report (DPR) has been taken up for 4 laning 
from Pharenda to Maharajganj and from Padrauna to Tamkuhiraj of 
NH-730 in length of 71 km.   DPR for 4 laning  from Bahraich to Sanai 
Chauraha, Maharajganj to K aptanganj & Kaptanganj to Padrauna of 
NH-730 in a length of 229 km has been included in Annual Plan 
2026-27.   

          The Government has also taken up studies for Shamli -
Gorakhpur High Speed Corridor, which is almost parallel to existing 
NH-730 with offset ranging from 0 to about 45 km. 
          Section of road connecting Lakhimpur to Sitapur is State 
Highway under the jurisdiction of State Government of Uttar 
Pradesh, which has been already developed to 4 Lane standards. 
          Sitapur to Lucknow section of NH-30 has also been developed 
to 4 Lane standards.  
          State Highway No. 90 connects Lakhimpur city (NH -730) to 
India-Nepal International Border at Gauriphanta Border.  State 
Government of Uttar Pradesh is responsible for its development and 
maintenance. 
No National Highway currently passes through the Dudhwa 
National Park. However, km 82.000 to 84.200 of NH -730 falls under 
the buffer zone, outside Dudhwa National Park. Upgradation of the 
above stretch from 2 Lane to 2 Lane with Paved shou lder was 
sanctioned under the work namely (Rehabilitation and upgradation 
of Khutar-Lakhimpur section from Km.82.00 to 140.00 of NH -730 to 
2L+PS). Stretch from Km.82.000 to 84.200 (width 7m) of NH-730 was 
not upgraded and was de -scoped as Forest clearance permission 
was not granted.   No proposal to construct elevated corridor or 
underpasses through the Dudhwa National Park is under 
consideration.

Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is considering enactment of legislation 
mandating periodic structural safety audits of high-rise buildings on the 
lines of statutory frameworks adopted in countries such as the United 
Kingdom and the Republic of Korea and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any national mechanism exists to monitor the cumulative 
long-term impact of seismic activity and ageing on the structural 
foundation strength of buildings and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the measures taken or proposed to mandate periodic post -
construction structural inspections for early detection of structural 
deterioration and prevention of building collapses; and 
(d) the timeline for framing and enforcing such legislation to detect 
early structural weakening, enhance public safety and prevent building 
collapse? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (d):  As per 12th Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban 
planning including building plan approvals and enforcement of building 
bye-laws, is the function of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban 
Development Authorities. Government of India supplements the efforts 
of the States through schematic interventions/ advisories. The  
…2/- 

-2- 
Government of India supplements the efforts of States and Union 
Territories through model regulations, technical standards, guidelines 
and advisories. The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has 
published Model Building Bye- laws (MBBL) – 2016 
(https://www.mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/07/0e33558a9326c8a89
f945cae00cc3647.pdf ), in which Chapter -6 deals with Provisions for 
Structural Safety, and lays down guidelines/standards relating to 
structural safety and seismic resilience of buildings. 
Further, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), under the Ministry of 
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India, 
has formulated various standards relating to earthquake resistant 
design and construction of buildings and structures,  and for seismic 
evaluation, repair and strengthening of buildings such as IS 1893 
(Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures), IS 4326:2013 
(Earthquake resistant design and construction of buildings – Code of 
Practice (third revision) and other allied codes for adoption and 
enforcement by States/UTs and Urban Local Bodies as part of their 
building regulations. 
Further, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), under the 
Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), has issued the National Disaster 
Management Guidelines on Management of Earthquakes, which provide 
guidance on earthquake risk reduction, including measur es for safer 
construction, structural strengthening and retrofitting of buildings, 
particularly lifeline and critical infrastructure 
(https://ndma.gov.in/sites/default/files/PDF/Guidelines/earthquakes.pdf). 
Regulation and enforcement relating to periodic structural and seismic 
safety audits, building inspection regimes and compliance 
requirements are within the domain of States/Union Territories (UTs) 
and ULBs.

Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the price of Brent crude oil has declined by nearly forty-four per cent from about 
126.41 US dollars per barrel on April, 30 to about 70.78 US dollars per barrel as on 2 July, 
2026, if so, the details thereof; and 
(b) whether the Government has taken any decision regarding the reduction in the prices of 
petrol and petroleum products including Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) proportionately, if 
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुर ेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) & (b): The price of Brent crude oil was USD 122.86/barrel on 30th April 2026 and 
USD 68.17/barrel on 2nd July 2026. However, the Brent crude prices continue to heavily 
fluctuate and have again increased to USD 92.19/barrel on 21st July 2026. India imports more 
than 88% of its crude oil requirements. Since March 2026, due to the West Asia crisis, 
international crude oil prices have risen significantly. To protect consumers from its impact, 
in March 2026, Government reduced the excise duties on petrol and diesel by Rs. 10 per litre 
each, resulting in a substantial negative impact on its tax revenues. 
The conflict in the West Asia has not abated and the resultant geopolitical situation continues 
to be highly volatile. PSU OMCs have incurred huge losses on the sale of petrol, diesel, LPG, 
etc. Against this, Petrol and Diesel prices were increased only marginally by the PSU OMCs. 
The current RSP of Petrol and Diesel are Rs.102.12 and Rs.95.20 per litre respectively 
(Delhi). 
Prices of LPG in the country are linked to its prices in the international market. Government 
continues to modulate the effective price to consumer for domestic LPG. 
Prior to the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East in February 2026, India used to import 
about 60 percent of its LPG consumption, out of which about 90 percent was transiting 
through the Strait of Hormuz. With the closure of Strait of Hormuz, supplies of imported 
LPG were severely constrained. The Government took a series of proactive measures to 
ensure stability in LPG supplies post the outbreak of the conflict. These include rapid 
increase in production of LPG from 34 to 54 TMT per day, prioritization of household usage 
of LPG, diversification of import sources, dynamic stock management, inter-regional 
allocation to address localized shortages, etc. Despite this unprecedented crisis, supply of 
LPG to all households in the country has been ensured without any disruption. During the 
peak of this crisis, more than 56 crore domestic LPG cylinders were delivered between 
March and June 2026, including more than 12 crore cylinders to Ujjwala families.  
 

 
 
With the onset of the West Asia crisis, the average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for 
LPG pricing) rose upto US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP 
rose further to US$ 796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 
14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder went to Rs.1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg 
cylinder, carrying an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of more than Rs 700 per 14.2 Kg 
cylinder, in June 2026. Even for the month of July 2026, the implicit subsidy on each 14.2 Kg 
domestic LPG cylinder is more than Rs 500 per cylinder. For more than 10.5 crore PMUY 
consumers, the effective price is only Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a targeted subsidy of 
Rs. 300 per cylinder, in addition to the implicit subsidy of more than Rs 500 per cylinder. 
Government have been ensuring availability of domestic LPG at affordable prices to 
households in the country for which Government have paid to the OMCs a compensation of 
Rs.22,000 crore in FY 2022-23 and paying Rs.30,000 crore during FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-
27. Even after the payment of this compensation, accumulated under-recovery of the PSU 
OMCs on domestic LPG was more than Rs 51000 crores as of 30th June 2026 itself.

SURVEY ON GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOODS 
883.  Dr. THIRUMAAVALAVAN THOLKAPPIYAN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has conducted any survey  regarding Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) 
during the last three years and if so, the details thereof; and 
(b) whether any early warning system has been insta lled to provide advance information regarding flood s 
based on the findings of such GLOFs survey and if s o, the details thereof along with the cost involved  in this 
regard? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a)    Yes. The Government of India has undertaken surveys and scientific assessments to identify and evaluate 
the risks associated with Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) in the Indian Himalayan Region. 
Central Water Commission (CWC) has identified sever al potentially dangerous glacial lakes for 
priority monitoring and currently monitors 2,485 gl acial lakes having an area greater than 10 hectares  across 
the Himalayan river basins, covering four States an d two Union Territories, during the period June to October 
every year using remote sensing techniques. 
Subsequently, the National Disaster Management Auth ority (NDMA), in collaboration with national 
scientific agencies, carried out scientific assessm ent of 189 high-risk glacial lakes across the India n 
Himalayan Region during 2025. Based on the assessme nt, 56 glacial lakes were classified as very high r isk 
considering their potential to trigger GLOFs and the exposure of downstream habitations and infrastructure.  
(b)    Based on the findings of the GLOF hazard assessm ents and glacial lake monitoring, the Government ha s 
initiated the establishment of GLOF Early Warning S ystems (EWS) at selected high-risk glacial lakes in  the 
Indian Himalayan Region.  
Further, NDMA is implementing the National GLOF Ris k Mitigation Programme (NGRMP), which 
was approved in 2024, for implementation in the Sta tes of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and 
Arunachal Pradesh at a total approved cost of Rs. 1 50 crore. The programme envisages Hazard and Risk 
Assessment, Monitoring and Early Warning Systems, s ite-specific structural and non-structural mitigati on 
measures, and community awareness and capacity building.   
However, at present, no end-to-end GLOF Early Warni ng System has been commissioned under the 
National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme.  
In addition, NDMA, in collaboration with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the 
Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority (SSDMA),  conducted multi-agency expeditions to the high-ris k 
South Lhonak and Shako Cho glacial lakes in Sikkim during 2023 and 2024 to facilitate scientific 
investigations and the development of appropriate m onitoring, early warning mechanisms and mitigation 
measures. 
An amount of Rs. 52.50 crore has been earmarked und er the Monitoring and Early Warning System 
component of the NGRMP, out of the total programme outlay of Rs. 150 crore.

As on 18.07.2026, all the 0.85 lakh rural households in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & 
Diu, are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. At present, Union Territory of DNH 
& DD is not availing central funds under JJM. 
Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation has informed 
that Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched during the year 2015 -
16 with the objective of enhancin g physical access of water on farms, expanding cultivable 
area under assured irrigation, improving on -farm water use efficiency, and promoting 
sustainable water conservation practices. 
Under PMKSY-AIBP, a total of 125 major and medium irrigation projects have been taken up. 
Of these, 71 projects have been completed. Since 2016, these projects have resulted in the 
creation of an additional irrigation potential of 30.66 lakh hectares and command area 
development covering 23.42 lakh hectares. 
Further, a Specia l Package for completion of 8 major and medium and 83 surface minor 
irrigation projects to address agrarian distress in Vidarbha and Marathwada and other

However, various measures undertaken by Central Government to promote recharge and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 885 
 ANSWERED ON 23/07/2026 
JAL JEEVAN MISSION IN BIHAR 
885. SHRI RAJA RAM SINGH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a)   whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission in 
flood-prone districts of Bihar and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of Functional Household Tap Connections presently non -functional, district 
wise; 
(c)   whether any special package has been sanctioned to restore damaged rural drinking water 
infrastructure following floods and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the total Central assistance released to Bihar under the Flood Management and Border 
Areas Programme during the last five years; and 
(e)   the details of the funds utilised on infrastructure building and humanitarian assistance, 
district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
 
(a) to (c) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under JJM, the responsibility of 
planning, approval, implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking water supply 
schemes lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the States by 
providing technical and financi al assistance.  Since August 2019, Government of India, in 
partnership with States, has been implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal to 
make provision of tap water supply to every rural household of the country.  
The Union Cabinet has approved the extension of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) period up to 
December 2028 with enhanced outlay and restructured implementation focusing on structural 
reforms in rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
The Department has shared the operational guidelin es of JJM 2.0 with States/UTs which 
provides that each scheme shall have an emergency continuity plan to ensure uninterrupted 
water supply during droughts, floods and other disruptions. Further, the implementation of the 

Page 2 of 2 
 
mission, including in flood -prone districts of Bihar, is reviewed regularly through periodic 
review meetings, field visits, video conferences and monitoring through the JJM-IMIS. 
At the start of the Mission, around 3.16 lakh (1.89 %) rural households were reported to have 
tap water connections in State of Bihar. So far, as reported by the State on JJM -IMIS, around 
1.57 crore rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 
19.07.2026, out of 1.67 crore rural households in the State, around 1.60 crore (95.71%) 
households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. The district-wise status of tap 
connections is available in public domain at the following link:  
https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx 
(d)  & (e) No special package has been sanctioned  by the Department of Drinking Water & 
Sanitation for restoration of rural drinking water infrastructure damaged due to floods in Bihar. 
As informed by Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation, 
flood management and anti -erosion schemes are formulated and implemented by concerned 
State Governments as per their priority. The Union Government supplements the efforts of the 
States by providing technical guidance and also promotional financial assistance for 
management of floods in c ritical areas. Union Government is implementing "Flood 
Management and Border Areas Programme (FMBAP)" 2 for providing central assistance to 
States for works related to flood control, anti-erosion, drainage development, anti-sea erosion, 
etc. The total central assistance released to Bihar under Flood Management and Border Areas 
Programme (FMBAP) during last five years is Rs. 295.728 crore.

carriageway, construction of underpasses/overpasses, etc. are also 
taken as permanent rectification measures of black corridors as per 
site requirement. Long term rectification works involve pre -
construction activities such as land acquisition, forest clearance & 
utility shifting which takes significant time.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 887 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
OPERATIONALISATION OF MORADABAD AIRPORT  
887.     MRS RUCHI VIRA                      
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite the completion of Moradabad 
Airport, regular commercial flight operations and cargo services have not yet been 
commenced therefrom, causing considerable inconvenience to exporters and if s o, 
the reasons therefor; 
(b) the present status of providing air connectivity from Moradabad to major 
commercial centres such as Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata under the UDAN Scheme; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish a dedicated Air Cargo Complex  
at Moradabad Airport for speedy export of brass handicrafts and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the time -bound plan/scheme of the Government to develop an aero -city in the 
nearby areas of the airport for generating employment opportunities for local 
youth? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): Moradabad Airport was identified and developed under the UDAN 
Scheme and is licensed for 2B -VFR operations. M/s Flybig has novated its 
contractual rights and obligations under the RCS to M/s Skyhop for the operation 
of the Moradabad to Lucknow route and other RCS routes connecting Kanpur, 
Hindon, Saharanpur and Dehradun.  
 
Under the next phase of the initiative, the Government has recently approved the 
next phase of the UDAN Scheme to connect 120 new destinations and facilitate 
travel for 4 crore passengers over the next ten years. Routes connecting Moradabad 
airport may be considered in the forthcoming bidding round under the modified 
UDAN Scheme, if any airline submits valid bids for the same. 

 
The development of cargo infrastructure at airports is a continuous process which 
is undertaken in a phased and demand -driven manner, aligned with actual cargo 
volumes, traffic potential and commercial viability. 
 
As per the provisions of UDAN scheme, airports developed under the scheme are 
no-frills airports with minimal infrastructure and facilities necessary to make them 
operational. The primary objective is to reduce construction and operational costs, 
thereby promoting regional connectivity to smaller towns and cities. The 
modernisation and further development of airport infrastructure is undertaken by 
the Airports Authority of India (AAI) or the respective airport operators based on 
traffic demand, commercial feasibility, and operational requirements.

                                            Basic Amenities in Tribal Areas 
  
891.   Shri Ram Shiromani Verma : 
  
 Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
                                               
(a)   whether there is a lack of basic amenities such as education, health, roads, drinking water, 
housing, and livelihood in the Tharu tribe-dominated and forest areas of Shravasti and 
Balrampur in Uttar Pradesh and if so, the steps being taken by the Government for their 
development;  
 (b)  whether there is any proposal by the Government to extend Eklavya Model Residential 
Schools, tribal hostels, scholarships and skill development schemes in these districts, and if so, 
the details thereof;  
 (c) whether the Government is providing training, marketing and financial assistance to the 
people of the Tharu tribe by involving them in handicrafts, minor forest produce, Self-Help 
Groups, agriculture and other traditional livelihoods and if so, the details thereof for the last 
three years; and 
 d) whether the Government is implementing any special action plan to ensure the holistic 
development of tribal areas and the participation of local tribal communities and if so, the 
details thereof with regard to Shravasti and Balrampur? 
  
  
                                                                ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
  
(a) The Hon' ble Prime Minister has launched a special mega multi-sectoral mission named 
“Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan” (DAJGUA) on 2nd October,2024 for 
saturation of critical gaps in tribal villages and habitations, interventions relating to education, 
health, skill development, roads, housing, drinking water, sanitation, livelihood and digital 
connectivity including Tharu tribe-dominated areas of Shravasti and Balrampur districts of 
Uttar Pradesh.The program aims at the holistic and sustainable development of tribal 
populations in tribal villages through the convergence of schemes of 17 ministries including 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ (MoTA ) with 25 interventions. The program encompasses a total 
of 63,843 villages in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks across all tribal-dominated villages in 26 
States and 4 Union Territories including 16 and 2 villages respectively in Balrampur & 
Shravasti districts of the State of Uttar Pradesh.

least 20,000 tribal persons, as per the 2011 Census. The EMRSs are to be at par with Navodaya
