GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.991 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
  
Nutritional Status of Women and Children 
991. Shri Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the nutritional status of women and children 
in the Kalahandi - Balangir-Koraput (KBK) districts of Odisha under POSHAN 2.0, if so, 
the details thereof, district-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has reviewed vacancies of Anganwadi Workers and Helpers 
in Koraput and Rayagada districts, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish additional One Stop Centres and Sakhi 
Niwas facilities in the tribal districts of Odisha, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any study on trafficking and migration of 
tribal women and adolescent girls from southern Odisha, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes special interventions for reducing anaemia, 
stunting/maternal mortality among Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in 
Koraput and neighbouring districts, if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (e) The status of the percentage of stunting, wasting, underweight and overweight 
among children as per Poshan Tracker is as follows (as on 30.06.2026): 
  
Sr. No District Children Measured  Stunting  Wasting  Underweight  Overweight 
1. Kalahandi 1,12,937 22% 3% 9% 2% 
2. Balangir 1,03,027 14% 1% 7% 0% 

3. Koraput 1,12,661 27% 3% 14% 1% 
  
  
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme wherein 
Central Government is responsible for overall policy and planning and States/UTs are 
responsible for day to day programme  implementation which includes timely filling up of 
the vacant positions at all levels for smooth functioning of the scheme. Regular 
VCs/meetings are held with the States/UTs to monitor the filling up of vacant positions at 
various levels. APIP meetings ar e held annually to have a thorough review of the 
implementation of scheme at ground level which includes monitoring of the vacant 
positions filled by the States/UTs and plan of action on the same. In order to streamline 
the process of recruitment, uniform retirement date of 30th April has been fixed for AWWs 
and AWHs for better resource management. 
The status of in-position AWWs and AWHs in Koraput and Rayagada districts as of June, 
2026 is given below: 
District AWCs 
Operational 
AWW in -
position  
AWH in-position 
Koraput 3397 3360 3060 
Rayagada 2087 2061 1848 
  
One Stop Centre: One Stop Centre (OSC) provides integrated and immediate support 
and assistance under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both 
in private and public spaces all across the country including tribal districts of Odisha. 
It provides services like medical aid, legal aid and advice, temporary shelter, police 
assistance and psycho -social counselling to needy women. Till 30th June, 2026, 985 
OSCs are operational in the country which have assisted over 15.80 lakh women in the  
country. In the State of Odisha, 35 OSCs are operational which have assisted over 48,416 
women. As the scheme is demand driven, the States and UTs are encouraged to set -up 
at least one OSC in each district and additional OSC(s) in those districts which ha ve 
higher rate of crime against women or have bigger geographical area and in aspirational 
districts. 
  
Sakhi Niwas Scheme: Sakhi Niwas Scheme (Working Women Hostel) under the 
overarching Mission Shakti, is a demand driven Centrally Sponsored Scheme, under 
which funds are released directly to the States/UTs for implementation of the scheme. 
The States/UTs assess their requirement as per local needs and proposals are approved 
by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) after discussion with States/UTs. The scheme 
aims to promote availability of safe and conveniently located accommodation for working 

women in urban, semi -urban and also in rural areas where employment opportunity for 
women exists. 
  
Under the Scheme, financial assistance is provided for running of Sakhi Niwas in rented 
premises for working women and for those women who are under training for job. 
Provision of Day Care Centre for children of the residents of the Sakhi Niwas is an 
important aspect of the scheme.   In this scheme, fund is provided for rental 
accommodation.  Component of construction has been discontinued.  
  
Presently, 575 Sakhi Niwas are functional across the country, including 16 Sakhi Niwas 
in Odisha.  
                                                                                        
As per National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) “Crime in India - 2024” report, 477 women 
were trafficked in the State of Odisha during the year 2024. 
To address the challenges of malnutrition, Anganwadi services, Poshan Abhiyaan and 
Scheme for Adolescent girls (of 14 -18 years in Aspirational Districts and North -Eastern 
region) have been subsumed under the umbrella Mission Saksham Anganwadi and 
Poshan 2. 0 (Mission Poshan 2.0). It is a Centrally Sponsored mission, where the 
responsibility for implementation of various activities lies with the States and UTs. The 
Mission is being implemented in all States and UTs in the country including Particularly 
Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in Koraput and neighbouring districts of Odisha. 
Under this Mission, Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), 
Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the 
nutrition norms contained in Schedule -II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. These  
norms have been revised in January 2023. The old norms were largely calorie -specific; 
however, the revised norms are more comprehensive and balanced in terms of both 
quantity and quality of supplementary nutrition based on the principles of diet diversity  
that provides for quality protein, healthy fats and micronutrients (Calcium, Zinc, Iron, 
Dietary Folate, Vitamin A, Vitamin -B6 and Vitamin B-12). Extra Supplementary Nutrition 
is provided to Severely Acutely Malnourished (SAM) children as per National Food 
Security Act, 2013 (NFSA). 
Ministry vide notification dated 12th September 2022 issued Integrated Nutrition Support 
Programme- Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan (2.0), Rules 2022 to regulate the 
entitlements specified under the provisions of National Food Security Act, 2013 for every 
pregnant woman and lactating mother, till six months after childbirth and every child in 
the age group of six months to six years. 
To encourage diet -diversity and consumption of wholesome local produce, Poshan 
Vatikas have been developed at AWCs.  Poshan Vatikas help  to meet the important 
dietary diversity gap that has been repeatedly revealed in different surveys by providing 
different fruits, nuts, herbs, medicinal plants and vegetables round the year. The main 
objective of introducing the concept of Poshan Vatika i s to encourage community 
members to cultivate local food crops in their backyards.  

Further, Ministry of Women & Child Development and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare 
have jointly released the Protocol for Management of malnutrition in Children to prevent 
and treat severely acute malnutrition in children and for reducing associated mo rbidity 
and mortality. The community -based approach involves timely detection and screening 
of children with severe acute malnutrition in the community, management for those 
without medical complications with wholesome, local nutritious foods at home and 
supportive medical care. The said protocol includes an appetite test and screening 
process for children aged 6 months to 6 years who are severely acute malnourished 
(SAM) or severely underweight (SUW). Post -screening, such children are referred to 
Nutrition Rehabilitation Centers (NRC) or hospital facilities for further care. 
Under this Mission, one of the major activities undertaken is Community Mobilization and 
Awareness Advocacy to educate people on nutritional aspects as adoption of good 
nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for behavioral change. State and UTs are 
conducting and reporting regular sensitization activities under Jan Andolans during 
Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada celebrated in the months of September and March-
April respectively. Community Based Events (CBEs) have served as a significant strategy 
in changing nutritional practices and all Anganwadi workers are required to conduct two 
Community Based Events every month. A total of 10.8 crore CBEs have been conducted 
from 2018 to  June 2026 and more than 150 crore Jan Andolan activities have been 
conducted since 2018 through 15 Jan Andolans. 
The Government of India implements Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy to reduce 
prevalence of anemia among six beneficiaries age group- children (6-59 months), children 
(5-9 years), adolescents (10-19 years), pregnant and lactating women and in women of 
reproductive age group (15-49 years) in life cycle approach through implementation of six 
interventions via robust institutional mechanism. These six interventions include 
Prophylactic Iron and Folic Acid supplementation (IFA Syrup provided biweekly to 
Children 6-59 months, IFA Pink tablets provided to Children 5 -9 years, IFA Blue tablets 
provided to Adolescent 1019 years, IFA Red tablets provided weekly to Women of 
Reproductive age group and IFA Red tablets daily for 180 days provided to pregnant 
women and la ctating mothers), Deworming (Pregnant women provided albendazole 
tablet in second trimester and all children provided albendazole tablets during National 
Deworming Day), Intensified Behavioural Change Communication campaign, Testing for 
anemia and treatment as per anemia management protocols, Mandatory provision of IFA 
fortified food in public health programmes and Addressing non nutritional causes of 
anemia especially malaria, fluoro sis and hemoglobinopathies. Additional interventions 
include digital interventions, active review and monitoring anaemic  beneficiaries with 
follow-up by ASHA, ANM at field level and IEC activities. Regular National level reviews, 
along with supportive supervision visits and Common Review Mission tours of the 
States/UTs are undertaken to support and strengthen the nutrition interventions across 
the country including districts with high prevalence of anemia. 
The ‘Poshan Tracker’ application was rolled out as an important governance tool. The 
Poshan Tracker facilitates monitoring and tracking of all AWCs, AWWs and beneficiaries 
on defined indicators. Technology under Poshan Tracker is being leveraged for dynamic 
identification of stunting, wasting, underweight prevalence among children. It has 
facilitated near real time data collection for Anganwadi Services such as, opening of 

AWCs, daily attendance of children, ECCE activities, Growth Monitoring of children, 
Provision of Hot Cooked Meal (HCM)/Take Home Ration (THR -not raw ration), Growth 
Measurement etc.The Poshan Tracker application is available here : 
https://www.poshantracker.in 
For last mile tracking of Service Delivery, Ministry of Women and Child Development 
(MWCD) has developed Facial Recognition System (FRS) in Poshan Tracker Application 
for distribution of Take-Home Ration to ensure that beneﬁt is given only to the intended 
beneﬁciary registered in Poshan Tracker. 
  
The Nominee Module has been introduced in Poshan Tracker to ensure uninterrupted 
delivery of Take -Home Ration (THR) to the beneficiaries; Pregnant Women, Lactating 
Mothers, and Adolescent Girls. If due to any reason, the registered beneficiary is unable 
to visit the Anganwadi Centre to receive their THR through FRS, she can nominate a 
nominee on her behalf to receive her THR.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 992 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 24TH JULY, 2026 
 
ACCESS TO JUSTICE OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES 
 
992. SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY: 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details regarding the legal aid services presently available for persons with disabilities, 
including the nature of assistance provided and the coverage thereof; 
(b) the details regarding the functioning, mandate and outreach of specialised Legal Services 
Units (ILUs) established for persons with mental illness and intellectual disabilities; 
(c) the details regarding the accessibility standards prescribed and implemented for judicial 
infrastructure, including courts, tribunals and legal service institutions, to ensure access 
for persons with disabilities; 
(d) whether e-Courts Phase-III provides for enhanced accessibility features for persons with 
disabilities, including digital accessibility, assistive technologies and inclusive design 
standards; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof, including the timelines for implementation and the monitoring 
mechanisms to ensure effective compliance? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) and (b): The Government has undertaken several measures to make available affordable, 
quality and speedy legal services to the common man, including persons with disabilities. The 
legal Services Authorities (LSA) Act, 1987 provides for free and competent legal serv ices to 
the weaker sections of the society including Persons with Disabilities. As per Section 12(d) of 
the LSA Act, 1987, “a person with disability as defined in clause (i) of section 2 of the Persons 

with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1955” 
is entitled to free legal aid. 
 
            NALSA is also implementing a specific Scheme for Persons with Disabilities named 
NALSA (Legal Services to Persons with Mental Illness and Persons with Intellectual 
Disabilities) Scheme, 2024. This Scheme aims to ensure that legal services are responsive to 
the specific legal and social needs of persons with mental illness and persons with intellectual 
disabilities. Under this Scheme, specialised ‘Legal Services Unit for Persons with Mental 
Illness & Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (LSUM) called ‘Manonyay’’ units have been 
established in all States/UTs except Lakshadweep.  The LSUM is the primary institutional 
mechanism for the del ivery of legal services to persons with mental illness and persons with 
intellectual disabilities at Mental Health Establishments, Police Stations, Courts, Railway 
Stations, Bus Stands, Beggar’s Homes, Women’s Protection Homes, Child Care Institutions, 
Prisons, Detention Centres, Front Offices and through Home Visits.  
 
           The details of the persons with disabilities provided legal services under the Legal 
Services Authorities Act, 1987 during the last three financial years is as under: 
 
Financial Year Number of persons with disabilities 
provided legal services 
2023-24 11,591 
2024-25 8,313 
2025-26  15,280 
 
(c): The Government is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for development of 
infrastructure facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts by augmenting the resources of 
the State  Governments/UTs for construction of Court Halls, Residential Units for Judicial 
Officers, Lawyers’ Hall, Digital Computer Rooms and Toilet Complexes. As per guidelines of 
the Scheme, the Sta tes/UTs ensures that the proposed infrastructure have disabled-friendly 
design. The building design are in conformity with the requisite norms/accessibility standards 
as laid down by Central Public Works Department , Department of Empowerment of Persons 
with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, from time to time. 
 

(d) and (e): The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner 
across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and 
Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. The eCommittee, Supreme Court of 
India is the  governing body that oversees the eCourts project and provides policy planning, 
strategic direction and guidance to the project for effective implementation of all components. 
Under eCourts Project Phase III, there are 24 components that have several significant 
measures devised to foster the creation of a robust and accessible digital infrastructure for 
citizens including persons with disabilities. Provision has been made for providing enhanced 
accessible ICT enabled facilities to persons with disabilities, at a budgetary outlay of Rs. 27.54 
crore and using S3WaaS platform (Secure, Scalable and Sugamya Website as a Service) that 
makes the website friendly for persons with disabilities, at a budgetary outlay of Rs. 6.35 crore. 
S3WaaS platform has features for easy visibility of content for partially and completely 
visually challenged citizens.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 993 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
 
Implementation of National AYUSH Mission 
 
993. Dr. D. Purandeswari 
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the systematic implementation of the National AYUSH Mission has expanded the 
network of traditional healthcare facilities across Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  if so, the total number of AYUSH Health and Wellness Centres/Ayushman Arogya 
Mandirs (AAMs) successfully operationalised in the State to provide free preventive healthcare 
during the financial year 2025-26; 
 
 
(c)  whether this proactive infrastructural development has measurably reduced the out -of 
pocket medical expenditures for rural families relying on alternative medicine; 
 
(d)  the details of the central financial allocations disbursed to the State Government for 
procuring high-quality Ayurvedic and Homeopathic medicines for these primary centres; and 
 
(e)  the steps proposed to integrate AYUSH healthcare facilities with the Ayushman Bharat 
Digital Mission (ABDM) for creation and integration of electronic health records for patients 
in Andhra Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
(a) and (b) Yes, as reported by the State, the systematic implementation of the National Ayush 
Mission (NAM) has significantly expanded and strengthened the network of traditional 
healthcare facilities across Andhra Pradesh as submitted below. 

  
 
 
126 Ayush Dispensaries have been upgraded as Ayush Health and Wellness Centers, 
now known as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Ayush) [AAM (Ayush)] are functional and are 
catering the needs of the public with upgraded facilities  with proper infrastructure and 
furniture to increase the out patients facilities.  
 
  Further, as reported by the State Government  of Andhra Pradesh , 
construction/renovation works have been carried out for 150 existing Ayush dispensaries that 
were in a dilapidated condition. The State has also reported completion of the construction of 
two new 50-bedded Integrated Ayush Hospitals at Kakinada and Visak hapatnam, to improve 
access to traditional medicine in the State, including in rural areas. 
 
(c) Yes, as reported by the State Government  of Andhra Pradesh , the patient flow has 
increased, resulting in greater utilization of Ayush services by the public. The State has further 
reported that the medical expenses for rural families has decreased as the Government is 
supplying medicines and providing healthcare services free of cost.  
As per the State's Annual Out-Patient Department (OPD) registry from April 2025 to March 
2026, an aggregate total of 1,162,527 Out -Patient (OP) consultations for Ayurveda, 844,578 
for Homoeopathy, and 212,003 for Unani systems were recorded in the dispensa ry segment 
alone. Additionally, dedicated Ayush hospitals registered an aggregated annual volume of 
247,336 OP visits (including 75,525 Ayurveda, 152,052 Homoeopathy, and 19,759 Unani 
cases). These interventions have contributed to strengthening and expand ing the network of 
traditional healthcare facilities in the State.   
 
(d) The State Government  of Andhra Pradesh  has reported that an amount of Rs. 22.16 
crores were allocated during the financial year 2025-26 for procurement of Ayush medicines 
including high quality Ayurvedic and Homoeopathic medicines. The sufficient  stocks of 
medicines procured and the dispensaries are well stocked with medicines to cater to the needs 
of the public attending these dispensaries. 
 
(e) The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) was launched by the Government of 
India in September 2021 to support the development of an integrated, citizen -centric national 
digital health ecosystem. As of 20th July 2026, 14,086 ABHAs and 43,298 ABHA linked 
records have been generated, including 723 ABHAs and 39,153 ABHA linked records in 
Andhra Pradesh, through the ABDM-enabled Ayush 1.0 and Ayush 2.0 applications. This will 
enable seamless digital cross-referrals and modern interoperable digital health reporting across 
Andhra Pradesh.  Further, Ayush Hospital Management Information System (AHMIS) has been 
developed under Ayush Grid project which is Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) 
compliant. Through the platform, patient registration, electronic health Records, referrals and 
continuity of care have been enabled digitally.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

REFORMS IN THE COUNTRY’S CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM  
994. SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has successfully implemented the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam with effect from 1 July 
2024, marking a historic reform of India's criminal justice system, if so, the overall progress of 
its implementation, State/UT-wise;  
(b) the number of police personnel, prosecutors and investigating officers trained under the 
new criminal laws, State/UT-wise;  
(c) the number of cases registered under major new provisions relating to organised crime, 
terrorism, electronic evidence and community service; 
(d) the measures taken to ensure a smooth transition from the previous legal framework, 
including integration with digital criminal justice platforms; and  
(e) the implementation status in Madhya Pradesh, particularly in Satna District, along with the 
future roadmap for strengthening citizen-centric criminal justice delivery? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a): Yes Sir, as per information provided by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) and the Bharatiya 
Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) came into force throughout the country with effect from 1 
July 2024.  
The States and Union Territories have taken necessary measures for their 
implementation, including issuance of relevant notifications and rules, adoption of digital 
applications and capacity building of stakeholders. 

2 
 
(b): Training of police personnel and other State-level stakeholders is primarily undertaken by 
the respective State and Union Territory Governments. In addition, the Bureau of Police 
Research and Development (BPR&D) has conducted capacity -building programmes a nd 
webinars for Master Trainers and other stakeholders across all 36 States and Union Territories. 
Since 2024, BPR&D has trained 83,740 officers and stakeholders from the five pillars of the 
criminal justice system, including Master Trainers. The cadre/position -wise, State/UT -wise 
and year-wise details are given in Annexure-I. The Master Trainers have also been utilised by 
State training institutions for conducting further training programmes within the respective 
States and Union Territories. The details of such training are given in Annexure-II. 
(c): As per the latest ‘Crime in India’ report released in 2024, the State/UT wise cases registered 
for organised crimes and terrorism are given in Annexure-III. 
The data related to the number of cases registered wherein the provision of electronic evidence 
and community service, were availed is not maintained  by the Ministry of Home Affairs.  
(d): The Nyaya Sanhitas has been implemented throughout the country with effect from 01 
July 2024, including the State of Madhya Pradesh. Further, ‘Police’, and ‘Public Order’ are 
State-list subjects as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. The responsibilities 
to maintain law and order, protection of life and property of the citizens including investigation 
and prosecution of crime and criminals rest with the respective State/UT Governments and are 
competent to deal with such offenses unde r the extant provisions of law, which also includes 
the implementation of the Nyaya Sanhita. However, the Central Government supplements their 
efforts by providing financial support for augmentation of criminal justice infrastructure under 
various schemes, including the Inter -Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) 2.0, Schemes 
for Modernisation of Forensic Capacities and Nirbhaya Fund-supported projects. 
(e): As per information provided by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, several steps have 
been taken for effective implementation of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Bharatiya 
Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 throughout the State, 
including Satna District. Judicial Officers have been imparted orientation and training through 
the Madhya Pradesh State Judicial Academy. Necessary amendments have been carried out in 
the Case Information System (CIS) and e -Courts software to facilitate implementation of the 
new criminal laws. The District Judiciary is regularly monitored through the administrative 
side of the High Court to ensure smooth transition and expeditious disposal of cases. The future 
roadmap includes continuous capacity building of Judicial Officers and court staff, 
strengthening digital court infrastructure, effective implementation of e -Courts P hase-III, 

3 
 
greater use of technology for case management, and improving accessibility, transparency and 
efficiency to provide citizen-centric criminal justice delivery.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 995
ANSWERED ON - 24/07/2026
CONSULAR AND LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO DETAINED FISHERMEN
995. SHRI SURESH KUMAR SHETKAR:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether consular and legal assistance is provided to fishermen  
detained in foreign prisons, if so, the details thereof and if not, the  
reasons therefor; 
(b) whether any delays have occurred in repatriation of fishermen after  
completion of legal formalities, if so, the details thereof and if not, the  
reasons therefor; 
(c) whether compensation or relief is provided to families of detained  
fishermen, if so, the details thereof including details of the scheme in  
this regard and if not, the reasons therefor; 

2
(d) whether technological support such as GPS devices is provided to  
fishermen to avoid boundary violations, if so, the details thereof and if  
not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e)  whether  coordination  exists  between  Central  and  State  
Governments to address fishermen detention issues, if so, the details  
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a) to (e) The Government of India attaches high priority to the safety,  
security and welfare of Indian fishermen. The Government has been  
taking up all fishermen related issues, including the early release and  
repatriation  of  Indian  fishermen  and  boats,  with  respective  
Governments through diplomatic channels, various official interactions 
and  established  bilateral  mechanisms.  In  all  interactions,  it  is 
conveyed  that  the  issues  related  to  fishermen  may  be  considered 
purely on humanitarian and livelihood grounds and that the use of  

3
force should be avoided in all circumstances. Further, Indian Missions  
and Consulates in the respective countries make regular visits to local  
jails  and  detention  centers  to  ascertain  the  condition  of  Indian 
fishermen  and  provide  requisite  help  and  support,  including  legal 
assistance. The Missions also provide necessary travel documents to  
facilitate repatriation of released fishermen to India.
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry  
and Dairying, Government of India runs various flagship programs for  
the welfare of fishermen. State Governments also run various relief  
schemes to provide financial assistance to the family members of the  
detained  fishermen.  A  JWG  on  Fisheries  which  includes  
representatives  of  various  stakeholders  at  Central  and  State  
Governments also meet regularly. 
The  Government  has  been  rolling  out  Vessel  Communication  and 
Support  System,  including  the  installation  of  transponders,  under 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), on approximately  
1,00,000 fishing vessels in coastal states and Union Territories. The  
two  way  communication  system  allows  for  sending  and  receiving 

4
emergency messages in cases of natural calamities and for alerting  
fishermen  if  they  unintentionally  cross  the  International  Maritime 
Boundary Line (IMBL).

(a) whether child malnutrition and anaemia have been assessed in Perambalur 
Parliamentary Constituency in Tamil Nadu, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the measures being taken to strengthen women's safety and One Stop

(c) the details of the steps taken to improve cyber safety awareness among women and

(d) the details of the initiatives to promote women's employment and self -help groups; 
and

in the said Constituency? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)

overweight among children in these districts as per Poshan Tracker App is as follows (as

(b) to (e) The ‘Mission Shakti’ aims at strengthening interventions for women safety, 
security and empowerment. It seeks to focus on proposing strategies for improving 
convergence across Ministries/ Departments and at different levels of governance. 
Mission Shakti comprises of two sub -schemes ‘Sambal’ and ‘Samarthya’ for safety and 
security of women and empowerment of women respectively. 
The “Sambal” sub-scheme is for safety and security of women. It has the components of 
One Stop Centres (OSCs), Women Helpline (WHL), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) 
and Nari Adalat.  
• One Stop Centre - One Stop Centre (OSC) provides integrated and immediate 
support and assistance under one roof to women affected by violence and those 
in distress, both in private and public spaces all across the country. It provides 
services like medical aid, legal aid and advice, temporary shelter, police assistance 
and psycho-social counselling to needy women. rural and economically weaker 
regions of the country. Till 30th June, 2026, 985 OSCs are operational in the 
country which have assisted over 15.80 lakh women in the country. As on date, 59 
OSCs are operational in Tamil Nadu. Out of which, one OSC in Karur, one OSC in 
Perambalur, and two OSCs in Tiruchirappalli are operational which have assisted 
over 1.82 lakh women. 

The scheme is Centrally Sponsored Scheme, and the Central Government 
provides 100% financial assistance to States and UTs. The overall implementation 
of scheme lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations. 
Further, once in a year, the Programme  Approval Board (PAB) monitors with 
States and UTs, the progress of activities under the scheme and reviews status of 
achievement of objectives and effective delivery of services to women and 
children. Apart from this, officials of the Ministry continuousl y review the scheme 
through meetings, video conferencing and by making field visits to States and UTs 
from time to time. 
• Women Helpline (WHL)- Women Helpline (WHL -181) provides 24-hour toll-free 
telecommunication services to support women in both emergency and non -
emergency situations. It offers assistance to women affected by violence and 
provides information about government schemes and servic es all across the 
country. 
• Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) - Beti Bachao Beti Padhao  (BBBP) Scheme 
was launched on 22nd January 2015 to help address Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and 
related issues of empowerment of girls and women over a life cycle continuum. 
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme has transformed from policy initiative 
into national movement by mobilizing various stakeholders, including government 
agencies, media civil society and general public. 
• Nari Adalat - Nari Adalat scheme provides a platform for alternative grievance 
redressal for women at the gram panchayat level. The Adalats are mandated to 
help women in distress at the panchayat level in resolving smaller issues relating 
to domestic violence, and other gender-based violence by negotiation, mediation, 
and reconciliation with mutual consent for accessible justice. 
  
Government has taken the following steps to reduce exposure of women and girls to 
cyber threats:  
i. Information Technology Act, 2000 (‘IT Act’) and the Information Technology 
(Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (‘IT Rules’). 
ii. Clear objective of online safety of users, particularly children.  
iii. Section 67B of the IT Act penalises electronic material depicting children in a 
sexually explicit, obscene, or indecent manner - Cognisable offence. Includes 
inducing them into online sexual relationships, facilitating abuse, or recording such 
acts. 
iv. Punishable with imprisonment of up to 5 years & up to ₹10 lakh fine on first 
conviction, and up to 7 years imprisonment with the same fine on subsequent 
convictions.  

v. Section 77A of the IT Act: For offences made compoundable under the Act (other 
than offences for which the punishment for life or imprisonment for a term 
exceeding three years has been provided), the court shall not compound the 
offence if it has been committed against a child below the age of 18 years. 
  
vii. Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“DPDP Act”)  
  
● Establishes the legal framework to regulate the processing of digital personal 
data. 
● Allows Data Fiduciaries to process the personal data of children only with 
parental consent  
● Does not permit processing of personal data which is detrimental to well -being 
of children or involves tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising 
  
viii.  Information Security Education & Awareness (“ISEA”) Programme  
  
● To generate awareness among users while using internet  
● Dedicated website has been created for information security awareness that 
generates and upgrades relevant awareness material on a regular basis  
● It can be accessed at https://staysafeonline.in/ 
  
ix. Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) 
  
● Regularly shares safety and security tips and awareness posters, info -graphics 
and videos on its official websites and social media handles  
  
● Aimed at sensitizing internet users on cyber security attacks and frauds including 
online safety measures for children.  
  
x. The Protection of Children Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012  was enacted to 
safeguard children from sexual offences and prevent such crimes against children. It 
provides punishment as per the gravity of offence.  

  
xi. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) , a statutory body 
under Ministry of Women and Child Development has prepared following guidelines on 
Cyber Safety and Protection of children:  
  
● Guideline and standard content for raising awareness among children, parents, 
educators and general public titled “Being Safe Online” is available at 
https://ncpcr.gov.in/public/uploads/16613370496305fdd946c31_being-safe-
online.pdf 
● Guidelines on Cyber Safety (for inclusion in) Manual on Safety and Security of 
Children in Schools which is available at: 
https://ncpcr.gov.in/uploads/16613369326305fd6444e1b_cyber-safety-
guidline.pdf 
● Guidelines for Schools for prevention of bullying and cyber bullying” which is 
available at https://ncpcr.gov.in/uploads/1714382687662f675fe278a_preventing -
bullying-andcyberbullying-guidelines-for-schools-2024.pdf 
● NCPCR has a dedicated/ transparent Online Complaint System 
https://ncpcr.gov.in/ebaalnidan/, to ensure timely/speedy redressal of complaints 
of various violations and deprivation of child rights 
  
xii. Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)  has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime Coordination 
Centre’ (I4C) as an attached office to deal with all types of cybercrime in the country, in a 
coordinated and comprehensive manner.  
  
xiii. ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’  (https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been 
launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types 
of cyber-crimes, with special focus on cyber-crimes against women and children. Cyber-
crime incidents reported on this portal, their conversion into FIRs and subsequent action 
thereon are handled by the LEAs of State/UT concerned, as per the provision of law. 
  
The “Samarthya” sub scheme of Mission Shakti is for empowerment of women. It has the 
components of Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), Shakti Sadan, Sakhi 
Niwas, Palna and SANKALP: Hub for Empowerment of Women (HEW). 
• Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) - The PMMVY is a Centrally 
Sponsored Maternity Benefit Scheme under which cash incentives of ₹5,000/ - is 
provided directly to the Bank/Post Office account of the beneficiary in Direct Benefit 

Transfer (DBT) mode for first child. The eligible beneficiaries receive the remaining 
cash incentive, as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani 
Suraksha Yojana after institutional delivery, so that on an average a woman gets 
₹6,000/-. Ca sh incentive of ₹6,000/ - is also provided under PMMVY to eligible 
beneficiaries for second child subject to the second child being a girl. 
  
• Sakhi Niwas Scheme: Sakhi Niwas Scheme (Working Women Hostel) under the 
overarching Mission Shakti, is a demand driven Centrally Sponsored Scheme, 
under which funds are released directly to the States/UTs for implementation of 
the scheme. The States/UTs assess their requireme nt as per local needs and 
proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) after discussion 
with States/UTs. The scheme aims to promote availability of safe and conveniently 
located accommodation for working women in urban, semi-urban and also in rural 
areas where employment opportunity for women exists.  
  
Under the Scheme, financial assistance is provided for running of Sakhi Niwas in 
rented premises for working women and for those women who are under training 
for job. Provision of Day Care Centre for children of the residents of the Sakhi 
Niwas is an important aspect of the scheme.  In this scheme, fund is provided for 
rental accommodation.  Component of construction has been discontinued.   
  
Presently, 575 Sakhi Niwas are functional across the country including 01 Sakhi 
Niwas in Perambalur district and 09 Sakhi Niwas in Tiruchirappalli district of Tamil 
Nadu.  
  
• Shakti Sadan Scheme: Under the overarching ‘Mission Shakti’, erstwhile 
schemes of ‘Swadhar Greh’ – Home for women in difficult circumstances and 
‘Ujjawala’- Home for women rescued from Trafficking, have been merged and are 
now known as ‘Shakti Sadan Scheme’, which is an Integrated Relief and 
Rehabilitation Home for women in distressful situations including trafficked 
women.  It aims at creating a safe and enabling environment for the women in such 
difficult situations, to enable them to overcome the adverse circumstances.  
  
The Shakti Sadan Scheme is a demand driven Centrally Sponsored Scheme, 
under which funds are  directly released to the States/UTs for implementation of 
the scheme.  The States/UTs assess their requirement as per local needs and 
proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) after discussion 
with States/UTs.  Under the Scheme, financial assistance is provided for running 
of Shakti Sadan in rented premises.    
   

Presently, 433 Shakti Sadans are functional across the country including 01 Shakti 
Sadan functional in Perambalur district of Tamil Nadu.   
  
  
• Palna Scheme: The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (AWCCs) under 
Palna Scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe 
and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers 
irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional support, health and 
cognitive develo pment of children, growth monitoring, immunization, education 
etc. Palna component under Samarthya vertical of Mission Shakti is a centrally 
sponsored scheme and is implemented with a funding ratio of 60:40 between 
Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & 
Special Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% 
funding will be provided by the Central Government.  
  
Palna is a demand driven scheme under which funds are  released to the 
States/UTs for implementation of the scheme.  The States/UTs assess their 
requirement and proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) 
after discussion with States/UTs.   
  
The Ministry continuously monitors implementation through periodic review 
meetings, video conferences, and field visits by Ministry officials to assess 
implementation and ensure effective delivery of services. In Tamil Nadu, 600 
AWCCs are approved as on 31.03.2026.   
  
• SANKALP: Hub for Empowerment of Women (HEW) - The SANKALP: HEW 
(Hub for Empowerment of Women) which functions as a Project Monitoring Unit 
(PMU) for all components of Mission Shakti. It serves as a single window system 
to bridge the information and knowledge gap regarding schemes and facilities 
available for women as well as guide them to avail the benefits and entitlements. 
  
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) under DAY-NRLM are to mobilize rural women into collectives 
to encourage savings and take up multiple livelihoods opportunities to increase household 
income and thereby reduce rural poverty.  
To enhance the efficiency of SHGs, The Ministry of Rural Development under DAY -
NRLM, is conducting awareness activities on nutrition, health and sanitation amongst 
SHG households through group meetings, community-based events, and mobilization to 
public he alth, nutrition and sanitation services with an aim to reduce out -of-pocket 
expenditure on health and improve quality of life. The training material issued by the line 
Ministries have been adapted in SHG context and are being used for discussions in the 

group meetings. SHG network is also supporting various national nutrition, health and 
sanitation campaigns. The IEC material shared by the host Ministry is circulated to the 
SHGs.  
  
To strengthen nutrition service delivery and promote Early Childhood Care and Education 
(ECCE), Saksham Anganwadis equipped with child friendly infrastructure compared to 
conventional AWCs, including facilities such as LED screens, water purifiers/RO 
machines, Poshan Vatikas , ECCE kits, and BALA (Building as Learning Aid) paintings 
have been established. 143 AWCs in the Perambalur district have been approved for 
upgradation of Saksham Anganwadi. Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) 
Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015) is the primary legislation for ensuring safety, security, dignity and 
well-being of children and is implemented by all the States and UTs including the State 
of Tamil Nadu. The Act creates statutory structures at the State and District levels which 
include Stat e Child Protection Society, Child Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice 
Boards (JJBs), District Child Protection Units. It also provides for establishment of Child 
Care Institutions (CCIs). There are 317 funded Child Care Institutions (CCIs) in the State 
of Tamil Nadu.

(a) & (b): The primary responsibility for development of infrastructure facilities for District and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 998 
ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
  
PROHIBITION OF CHILD MARRIAGE ACT, 2006 
998. Dr. Mohammad Jawed: 
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether child marriage continues to be reported from several parts of the country despite the 
enforcement of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the number of reported cases of child marriage, along with the number of prosecutions and 
convictions during the last five years, State/UT-wise; 
(c)  the details of the schemes, awareness campaigns and community -based interventions being 
implemented by the Government to prevent child marriage and to ensure girls remain in 
school; and  
(d)  whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the socio -economic factors 
contributing to child marriage, if so, the details of the corrective measures being taken to 
achieve the elimination of child marriage in line with Sustainable Development Go al 
5.3?           
  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
 
  
(a) to (d): The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) under Ministry of Home Affairs compiles 
and publishes data on cases of child marriage registered under the Prohibition of Child Marriage 
Act (PCMA), 2006 in its annual publication Crime in India. The report is available up to the year 
2024, as per the information available with NCRB, the number of cases chargesheeted, cases 
convicted, persons arrested, persons chargesheeted and persons convicted under the PCMA during 
the last five years in the country, State/UT-wise details is at Annexure.  

The Government of India has enacted ‘The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006’ (PCMA) to 
prevent and curb child marriages and to take punitive action against those associated with the 
solemnisation of child marriages. Section 16 of the PCMA authorises t he State Government to 
appoint for the whole State, or such part thereof as may be specified, an officer or officers to be 
known as the 'Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPO)' having jurisdiction over the area or 
areas specified in the notification. T his section also specifies the functions to be discharged by 
CMPOs, which include preventing solemnisation of child marriages by taking such action as they 
may deem fit; to collect evidence for the effective prosecution of persons contravening the 
provisions of the Act; to advise the individuals or counsel the residents of the locality not to indulge 
in promoting, helping, aiding or allowing the solemnisation of child marriages; to create awareness 
about the ill effects of child marriages; and to sensitize the community on the issue of child 
marriages. All these authorities function under the direct administrative control and supervision of 
respective State Governments and UT Administrations. 
Further, to strengthen implementation of the Act and accelerate progress towards elimination of 
child marriage in line with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5.3, the Government launched a 
national campaign ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat on 27th November 2024, with the objective of making 
India child -marriage-free. It is one of the most important imperatives to promote education, 
skilling, enterprise and entrepreneurship among girls and women to realise the vision of a ‘Viksit 
Bharat’ through ‘whole of government’  and ‘whole of society’ approach. The campaign aims to 
create awareness for prevention of child marriage, enhance involvement of parents, families, and 
communities, strengthen the role and capacity of CMPOs, encourage timely reporting of child 
marriage cases and identify adolescent girls who are school dropouts or at risk of child marriage 
to ensure their education, skilling and empowerment.  
To commemorate the success of the campaign and further intensify efforts, a 100 Days Special 
Campaign under Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat was launched on 4th December 2025 to mobilise all 
stakeholders in a structured and time-bound manner. The 100 Days Special Campaign focused on 
targeted outreach to institutions, community leaders and service provider, along with mandatory 
uploading of details of Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs) on the BVMB Portal.  
The campaign followed a spell-wise thematic implementation plan. Spell–I (27th November, 2025 
to 31st December, 2025) focused on sensitisation activities in schools, colleges and universities 
through debates, essay competitions and pledge ceremonies. Spell –II (1st January, 2026 to 31st 
January, 2026) focused on engagement with religious institutions and marriage -related service 
providers, including temples, mosques, caterers, tent houses and DJs, to discourage child marriage 
and display IEC materials. Spell –III (1st February, 2026 to 8th March, 2026) focused on 
mobilisation of Gram Panchayats and Municipal Wards for passing resolutions declaring their 
jurisdictions as child marriage free. 
 A dedicated digital platform, the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat portal 
(https://stopchildmarriage.wcd.gov.in), facilitates reporting of child marriage incidents, 

dissemination of information, and registration of pledges. Citizens, institutions, and public 
representatives can take the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat pledge on the dedicated portal as well as 
through the MyGov portal, promoting wide participation. Awareness pro grammes have reached 
over 12.2 crore citizens, and more than 42 lakh pledges against child marriage have been registered 
on the portal, reflecting strong community engagement and active participation across the country. 
The BVMB portal serves as a centrali sed repository of more than 68,900 CMPOs across States 
and Union Territories. This provides citizens with an efficient reporting mechanism, where early 
reporting enables timely intervention to prevent child marriages.  
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) Scheme was launched on 22nd January 2015 to help address 
Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of empowerment of girls and women over a life cycle 
continuum. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme has transformed from a policy initiative into 
a national movement by mobilizing various stakeholders, including government agencies, 
communities, media, civil society and the public at large. This movement aims not only to address 
immediate concerns related to sex ratio and gender-based discrimination but also to foster a 
cultural shift towards valuing the girl child and ensuring her rights and opportunities.  
The BBBP scheme focuses on creating mindset and behavioural changes towards the girl child by 
informing, influencing, motivating, engaging and empowering various stakeholders. To address 
this, Ministry has developed and circulated to all States and UTs, an  operational manual which 
inter-alia includes a thematic calendar for suggested convergence activities at district level with 
month wise specific themes for holistic development of the Girl Child and to ensure year -round 
engagement of girls, their families and communities. 
Further, preventing child marriage is a critical mandate under the Juvenile Justice (Care and 
Protection of Children) Act, 2015, wherein a child at imminent risk of marriage before attaining 
the legal age is defined as a “child in need of care and protection.” The Child Welfare Committees 
(CWCs), empowered under Sections 27–30 of the Act, are entrusted to take decisions in the best 
interest of such children, ensuring their safety, dignity, and well -being. The Ministry of Women 
and Child Development, through its Centrally Sponsored Scheme Mission Vatsalya, supports both 
institutional and non-institutional care services, including sponsorship, foster care, and after care, 
to safeguard vulnerable children. Emergency outreach is further strengthened through the 24x7 
Child Helpline (1098), integrated with ERSS -112, to provide immediate assistance in cases of 
child marriage risk. While the Ministry provides policy and programmatic support, the 
responsibility to prohibit and prevent child marriages lies primarily wi th the respective State and 
Union Territory governments, as ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the 
Constitution, making them competent to act against such offences under existing laws.

†999. Shri Anil Firojiya: 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the funds sanctioned and expenditure incurred by the Ministry in the Ujjain 
Parliamentary Constituency during the last five years;  
(b) the total number of AYUSH Health and Wellness Centres currently operating in the said 
constituency;  
(c) the total number of farmers in Ujjain provided assistance for the cultivation of medicinal 
plants;  
(d) whether there is any proposal for setting up an AYUSH Hospital/College in Ujjain and if

(e) the details of the future action plan of the Government for the expansion of AYUSH 
services in Ujjain? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH  
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 
(a) Under National Ayush Mission (NAM), as per the proposals received from the State 
through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs), an amount of Rs. 31439.679 lakhs has been 
allocated/ released as Central Share to State of Madhya Pradesh during the last five years. The 
State Government has reported an expenditure of Rs. 31439.679 lakh against this allocation. 
As reported by State Government of Madhya Pradesh, the details of the funds sanctioned and 
expenditure incurred in the Ujjain Parliamentary Constituency during the last five years is 
furnished at Annexure.

as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush) [AAM(Ayush)]  are operational in the said 
constituency.
